Thus it is said: the sage king's way of controlling foreign peoples rests fundamentally not on intimidating force but on virtue…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
業其具不在兵食而在紀綱
王之藎臣無念爾祖
童承敘
同考試官訓導胡批周公告君之意發揚殆盡莊
重若此篇者可多得耶
同考試官教諭周批雅頌夫人而能言也場中日晷
有限求溫雅無痕鑿此最難者取以冠本房
考試官教諭劉批文以理為主氣為輔此是作者
考試官學正孫批雅義不多見宜錄以傳
===
周公呼王臣而諭以當念先德其望於王者至
矣夫商士助周之祭文王之德誠可念也周公
不斥言於成王而託之臣不亦婉乎周公作詩
以戒成王此呼藎臣以告之曰我周有得天下
之事而尤有保天下之道凡爾王之藎臣錄名
于朝無一念不在其君忠愛之篤進進不止而
以安危爲己任者食人之祿無一時不顧其君
贊相之謀翼翼無怠而以休戚爲己責者今觀
膚大而敏達殷之士焉其不事周可也天眷爾
punctuated:
業，其具不在兵食，而在紀綱。
「王之藎臣，無念爾祖。」
童承敘
同考試官訓導胡批：周公告君之意，發揚殆盡。莊重若此篇者，可多得耶？
同考試官教諭周批：雅頌，夫人而能言也。場中日晷有限，求溫雅無痕鑿，此最難者，取以冠本房。
考試官教諭劉批：文以理為主，氣為輔，此是作者。
考試官學正孫批：雅義不多見，宜錄以傳。
周公呼王臣，而諭以當念先德，其望於王者至矣。夫商士助周之祭，文王之德誠可念也。周公不斥言於成王，而託之臣，不亦婉乎？周公作詩以戒成王，此呼藎臣以告之曰：「我周有得天下之事，而尤有保天下之道。凡爾王之藎臣，錄名于朝，無一念不在其君，忠愛之篤，進進不止，而以安危爲己任者；食人之祿，無一時不顧其君，贊相之謀，翼翼無怠，而以休戚爲己責者。今觀膚大而敏達，殷之士焉，其不事周可也。天眷爾
translation_en:
…virtuous achievement; its instruments lie not in troops and provisions, but in the principles and order of government.
“You devoted ministers of the king, do you not remember your ancestor?”
Tong Chengxu
Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Assistant Instructor: The Duke of Zhou’s intention in admonishing his ruler is brought out almost exhaustively. Can many essays as dignified as this be found?
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Anyone can discourse on the Odes and Hymns. But with the limited hours available in the examination hall, achieving a gentle elegance without traces of forced craftsmanship is the hardest thing. I select this as the best in my examining section.
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: Writing takes principle as its chief element and vital force as its support. This is the work of an accomplished writer.
Comment by Examiner Sun, School Instructor: Such an interpretation of the Odes is seldom seen; it should be recorded and transmitted.
The Duke of Zhou called upon the king’s ministers and instructed them to remember their forebear’s virtue: his expectations of the king were of the highest order. The men of Shang assisted in Zhou’s sacrifices; truly, King Wen’s virtue deserved remembrance. The Duke of Zhou did not address King Cheng directly, but entrusted his message to the ministers. Was this not tactful? The Duke of Zhou composed this poem to admonish King Cheng. Here he calls upon the devoted ministers and tells them: “Our Zhou has achievements by which it gained All under Heaven, and, still more importantly, a Way by which to preserve it. All you devoted ministers of the king whose names are enrolled at court never direct a single thought away from your ruler. Your profound loyalty and affection advance unceasingly, and you take responsibility for his security or peril. Receiving your ruler’s emoluments, you never for a moment cease to attend to him. In your plans to assist him, you are reverent and tireless, taking his fortunes and misfortunes as your own responsibility. Now consider those men of Yin, eminent and discerning: they might well have refrained from serving Zhou. Yet Heaven cherished your …

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
祖之德而我周之京有是裸獻是可監者也能
無念爾祖之德乎黼裳而哿冠殷之制焉其在
殷廟可也天釋有商之命而我周之廟有是常
服此可警者也得弗思文王之德乎文王既没
矣其緝熈之敬昭于天而不昧當知所以念之
而弗懈于脩有弗念焉則天道之去就未可知
而所謂商臣者不能常走我周之廟矣純德之
譽傳于時而不已當知所以思之而允迪于行
有弗思焉則人心之去留未可信而所謂商服
===
者不能恒在我周之庭矣吁周公以此戒王而
不敢斥言非啓導之深意也哉抑此詩當周公
制作天下盈成之時乃深陳絕商之禍以警之
者蓋君子在朝則常有亂世之言使人主多憂
而善心生小人則常有治世之言使人主多樂
而怠心生况周公身任天下之重恐成王不法
祖以墜厥宗而無以副託孤之責故見之書有
曰毋若殷王紂公之竭忠對越上天者如此豈
以禍商之事為可諱而不之進也哉後世稱守
punctuated:
祖之德，而我周之京有是裸獻，是可監者也。能無念爾祖之德乎？黼裳而哿冠，殷之制焉，其在殷廟可也。天釋有商之命，而我周之廟有是常服，此可警者也。得弗思文王之德乎？文王既没矣，其緝熈之敬昭于天而不昧，當知所以念之而弗懈于脩。有弗念焉，則天道之去就未可知，而所謂商臣者不能常走我周之廟矣。純德之譽傳于時而不已，當知所以思之而允迪于行。有弗思焉，則人心之去留未可信，而所謂商服者不能恒在我周之庭矣。
吁！周公以此戒王而不敢斥言，非啓導之深意也哉？抑此詩當周公制作、天下盈成之時，乃深陳絕商之禍以警之者，蓋君子在朝則常有亂世之言，使人主多憂而善心生；小人則常有治世之言，使人主多樂而怠心生。况周公身任天下之重，恐成王不法祖以墜厥宗，而無以副託孤之責，故見之書有曰：「毋若殷王紂。」公之竭忠對越上天者如此，豈以禍商之事為可諱而不之進也哉？後世稱守
translation_en:
…the virtue of your ancestor, and in the capital of our Zhou these men offer libations: here is a lesson to heed. Can you fail to remember your ancestor’s virtue? Robes embroidered with axe patterns and ornate caps [?] belong to the institutions of Yin; their presence in the ancestral temple of Yin would be fitting. Yet Heaven has withdrawn the mandate of Shang, and these customary vestments now appear in the ancestral temple of our Zhou: here is cause for vigilance. Can you fail to reflect upon King Wen’s virtue? King Wen has already passed away, but his reverence, continuously cultivated and made radiant, shines in Heaven without dimming. You should understand how to keep it in mind and never slacken in cultivating yourself. If you fail to remember it, there is no knowing whether Heaven’s favor will depart or remain, and those whom we call the ministers of Shang will not always hasten to serve in our Zhou ancestral temple. His reputation for pure virtue continues to circulate in the world without ceasing. You should understand how to reflect upon it and faithfully follow it in your conduct. If you fail to reflect upon it, there is no assurance that the people’s allegiance will remain rather than depart, and those whom we call the wearers of Shang vestments will not forever be present at our Zhou court.
Ah! The Duke of Zhou admonished the king in this way, yet did not venture to address him explicitly. Does this not reveal his profound purpose in guiding him? Moreover, this poem dates from the time when the Duke of Zhou established institutions and the realm enjoyed full prosperity and settled order. That he nevertheless set forth at length the calamity that extinguished Shang, to put the king on his guard, was because gentlemen at court constantly speak of times of disorder, causing the ruler to feel greater concern and thus giving rise to good intentions; petty men constantly speak of times of good order, causing the ruler to take greater pleasure and thus giving rise to indolence. Furthermore, the Duke of Zhou himself bore the weighty responsibility for the realm. He feared that King Cheng might fail to emulate his ancestor and bring down his ancestral house, leaving the duke unable to fulfill the responsibility entrusted to him for the orphaned heir. Thus we find these words in the Book of Documents: “Do not be like Zhou, king of Yin.” Such was the duke’s utmost loyalty in reverently responding to Heaven. How could he have considered the events that brought calamity upon Shang something to avoid mentioning, and therefore failed to present them to the king? Later generations, speaking of preserving …

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
成業而成治者莫如成王而周公相天下之功
於是章矣
春秋
齊侯鄭伯盟于石門隱公三年鄭伯髠頑
如會襄公七年
張珩
同考試官教諭武批胡傳論春秋名不名之意
甚明讀者類忽之此篇大議特出新奇且反覆百數
言無一贅字當未可以時文觀也錄之以式
考試官教諭劉批詞意高古錄之
考試官學正孫批得謹嚴體
春秋於諸侯有所以不名者有所以必名者甚矣
春秋之正名也諸侯不名於生而名於卒焉其皆
有深意乎且諸侯未始不策名矣石門之盟齊之
禄父鄭之寤生非諸侯乎會盟嘗名之載書矣聘
問亦名之簡牘矣今而獨不名焉豈史失而經因
之耶曰非也生而不名者禮也蓋禮莫先於名諸
侯之於大夫而大夫生則獨名者以其臣於人耳
punctuated:
成業而成治者，莫如成王，而周公相天下之功於是章矣。

春秋

齊侯、鄭伯盟于石門，隱公三年。鄭伯髠頑如會，襄公七年。

張珩

同考試官教諭武批：胡傳論春秋名不名之意甚明，讀者類忽之。此篇大議特出新奇，且反覆百數言，無一贅字，當未可以時文觀也。錄之以式。

考試官教諭劉批：詞意高古，錄之。

考試官學正孫批：得謹嚴體。

春秋於諸侯，有所以不名者，有所以必名者。甚矣，春秋之正名也！諸侯不名於生，而名於卒焉，其皆有深意乎？且諸侯未始不策名矣。石門之盟，齊之禄父、鄭之寤生，非諸侯乎？會盟嘗名之載書矣，聘問亦名之簡牘矣。今而獨不名焉，豈史失而經因之耶？曰：非也。生而不名者，禮也。蓋禮莫先於名，諸侯之於大夫，而大夫生則獨名者，以其臣於人耳。
translation_en:
…the inherited enterprise and achieving good government, none equaled King Cheng. Thus the Duke of Zhou’s achievement in assisting the governance of all under Heaven became manifest.

Spring and Autumn Annals

“The Marquis of Qi and the Earl of Zheng made a covenant at Shimen.” Third year of Duke Yin. “Kunwan, Earl of Zheng, went to the meeting.” Seventh year of Duke Xiang.

Zhang Heng

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: Hu’s Commentary explains very clearly the intention behind the Spring and Autumn Annals’ use or omission of personal names, yet readers generally overlook it. This essay’s main argument is exceptionally fresh and original. Moreover, although it develops the point repeatedly over a hundred-odd words, it contains not a single superfluous word. It should certainly not be regarded merely as a conventional examination essay. Selected as a model.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: Its language and ideas are lofty and antique. Selected for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Sun, School Director: It achieves a scrupulous and rigorous style.

In its treatment of the feudal lords, the Spring and Autumn Annals has reasons for withholding their personal names and reasons for necessarily recording them. How exacting the Annals is in rectifying names! It does not give the feudal lords’ personal names during their lifetimes, but does so at their deaths. Might there be profound intentions behind both practices? After all, it was never the case that the feudal lords’ personal names were not entered in records. At the covenant at Shimen, were Lufu of Qi and Wusheng of Zheng not feudal lords? At meetings and covenants, their names were indeed written in the covenant documents; in diplomatic exchanges, their names were likewise written on tablets. Why, then, are their names omitted here alone? Was this an omission in the historical records that the Classic simply followed? I say: no. To withhold their personal names during their lifetimes accords with ritual propriety. In ritual propriety, nothing takes precedence over names. As for the distinction between feudal lords and grand masters, the latter alone are named during their lifetimes because they serve as subjects of others. …

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
諸侯何人而可與大夫等乎以貴則辟公也以富
則一國也彼其命大夫如單伯如祭仲生猶不名
況諸侯乎吾故知春秋不名齊鄭者非私之也不
欲以大夫處諸侯蓋禮之中也夫諸侯固不當名
矣于鄟之會鄭之髠頑未至而卒非諸侯乎猶祿
父之侯于齊也猶寤生之伯于鄭也今而卒獨名
焉豈昔貴而今賤之耶曰非也卒而名之者亦禮
也蓋禮莫嚴於名諸侯之於天子而天子赴不以
名者以其大一統耳諸侯何人而敢與天子擬乎弔
===
賻皆同盟也葬送皆友邦也彼其首霸如齊桓如
晋文卒猶以名況他國乎吾又知春秋必名髠頑
者非薄之也不敢以天子處諸侯亦禮之中也吁
同一諸侯惟其不名也然後有以異於下而不替惟
其必名也然後可以別於上而不陵或抑或揚何莫
而非以禮為世道計哉嗟夫齊鄭不名然矣語石門
之盟已淪於傾危之習髠頑名之然矣迹會鄟之志
不失為禮義之君於戲二公巳矣髠頑不沒於從夷
而沒於從夏百世之下史策書之其將不泯乎
punctuated: 諸侯何人，而可與大夫等乎？以貴則辟公也，以富則一國也。彼其命大夫，如單伯，如祭仲，生猶不名，況諸侯乎？吾故知春秋不名齊鄭者，非私之也，不欲以大夫處諸侯，蓋禮之中也。夫諸侯固不當名矣，于鄟之會，鄭之髠頑未至而卒，非諸侯乎？猶祿父之侯于齊也，猶寤生之伯于鄭也。今而卒獨名焉，豈昔貴而今賤之耶？曰：非也。卒而名之者，亦禮也。蓋禮莫嚴於名，諸侯之於天子，而天子赴不以名者，以其大一統耳。諸侯何人，而敢與天子擬乎？弔賻皆同盟也，葬送皆友邦也。彼其首霸，如齊桓，如晋文，卒猶以名，況他國乎？吾又知春秋必名髠頑者，非薄之也，不敢以天子處諸侯，亦禮之中也。吁！同一諸侯，惟其不名也，然後有以異於下而不替；惟其必名也，然後可以別於上而不陵。或抑或揚，何莫而非以禮為世道計哉！嗟夫！齊鄭不名，然矣；語石門之盟，已淪於傾危之習。髠頑名之，然矣；迹會鄟之志，不失為禮義之君。於戲！二公巳矣，髠頑不沒於從夷，而沒於從夏。百世之下，史策書之，其將不泯乎？
translation_en: What standing do the feudal lords possess, that they could be placed on the same footing as grandees? In rank, they are territorial lords; in wealth, they possess an entire state. Even royally commissioned grandees such as Shan Bo and Zhai Zhong are not referred to by personal name during their lifetimes; how much more should this apply to feudal lords? Thus I know that when the Spring and Autumn Annals omits the personal names of the rulers of Qi and Zheng, it does not show them favoritism. It refuses to treat feudal lords as grandees: this accords with the proper measure of ritual. Certainly, then, feudal lords ought not to be named. Yet at the meeting at Zhuan, Kunwan of Zheng died before arriving. Was he not a feudal lord? He was just like Lufu, who ruled Qi as marquis, or Wusheng, who ruled Zheng as earl. Why, then, is he specifically named at his death? Does this mean that he was honored before but is now demeaned? I say: no. Naming him at death likewise accords with ritual. For in ritual, nothing is more strictly regulated than the use of personal names in the relationship of feudal lords to the Son of Heaven. The Son of Heaven is not personally named in the announcement of his death because supreme importance is attached to unified rule. What standing do feudal lords possess, that they dare compare themselves with the Son of Heaven? Those who offer condolences and contributions toward funeral expenses are all fellow members of their covenant; those who attend their burial and funeral procession are all friendly states. Even the foremost hegemons, such as Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin, are personally named at death; how much more should this apply to rulers of other states? Thus I also know that when the Spring and Autumn Annals insists on naming Kunwan, it does not disparage him. It does not presume to treat a feudal lord as the Son of Heaven: this, too, accords with the proper measure of ritual. Ah! These are the very same feudal lords: only by omitting their personal names can they be distinguished from those below them without degradation; only by requiring their personal names can they be distinguished from the sovereign above them without usurpation. Whether lowering or elevating them, how could any of this fail to use ritual to safeguard the moral order of the world? Alas! It is indeed proper that the rulers of Qi and Zheng are not personally named; yet, speaking of the covenant at Shimen, they had already sunk into practices of intrigue and peril. It is indeed proper that Kunwan is personally named; yet, examining his intention to attend the meeting at Zhuan, he still qualifies as a ruler devoted to ritual and righteousness. Alas! Enough of those two dukes! Kunwan died not while following the Yi peoples, but while following the Xia states. A hundred generations hence, with this written in the historical records, will his memory not endure?

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
齊侯衛侯胥命于蒲桓公三年盟于召陵僖
公四年
嚴志迪
同考試官教諭武批此篇比兩傳不盟不戰立
論而孔子志大道之行與三代之英之意發揮殆盡
詞甚俊逸亦時文中之傑出者矣佳士佳士
考試官教諭劉批文有起伏可錄
考試官學正孫批語意自別
信以相喻者春秋固善之禮以勝敵者春秋尤美
===
之此齊衛之胥命于蒲桓公之盟于召陵皆春秋
僅見者也聖人樂與人爲善安得不特書之哉愚
嘗聞屢盟長亂之訓而嘆大道之不可復矣孰謂
春秋之初乃有不盟而喻如胥命于蒲者乎斯時
也齊僖欲伯于東衛宣欲伯于北瓦屋之參盟怨
隙雖釋東門之分黨敵勢猶存使懷疑者處此孰
不曰必歃血而後定哉而二公不然衛命齊以牧
伯而彼之心已信齊推衛以雄長而此之心無疑
雖曰自相命伯非盛世所欲聞然盟誓紛紜之秋
punctuated:
齊侯、衛侯胥命于蒲，桓公三年。盟于召陵，僖公四年。
嚴志迪。
同考試官教諭武批：此篇比兩傳不盟、不戰立論，而孔子志大道之行與三代之英之意，發揮殆盡。詞甚俊逸，亦時文中之傑出者矣。佳士！佳士！
考試官教諭劉批：文有起伏，可錄。
考試官學正孫批：語意自別。
信以相喻者，春秋固善之；禮以勝敵者，春秋尤美之。此齊衛之胥命于蒲、桓公之盟于召陵，皆春秋僅見者也。聖人樂與人爲善，安得不特書之哉？愚嘗聞屢盟長亂之訓，而嘆大道之不可復矣。孰謂春秋之初，乃有不盟而喻如胥命于蒲者乎？斯時也，齊僖欲伯于東，衛宣欲伯于北。瓦屋之參盟，怨隙雖釋；東門之分黨，敵勢猶存。使懷疑者處此，孰不曰必歃血而後定哉？而二公不然。衛命齊以牧伯，而彼之心已信；齊推衛以雄長，而此之心無疑。雖曰自相命伯，非盛世所欲聞，然盟誓紛紜之秋，
translation_en:
“The Marquis of Qi and the Marquis of Wei mutually acknowledged one another at Pu.” Third year of Duke Huan. “They covenanted at Shaoling.” Fourth year of Duke Xi.
Yan Zhidi.
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: This essay builds its argument by comparing the two commentarial accounts concerning the absence of a covenant and the absence of battle. It develops almost exhaustively Confucius’s longing for the practice of the Great Way and for the outstanding men of the Three Dynasties. Its language is exceptionally elegant and spirited; it is an outstanding example of contemporary examination prose. A fine scholar! A fine scholar!
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: The composition has rises and falls and merits inclusion.
Comment by Examiner Sun, School Instructor: Its language and ideas are distinctive.
The Spring and Autumn Annals certainly approves of those who reach mutual understanding through good faith; it praises still more those who overcome an enemy through ritual propriety. The mutual acknowledgment of Qi and Wei at Pu and Duke Huan’s covenant at Shaoling are both occurrences rarely seen in the Spring and Autumn Annals. The Sage delighted in helping others to do good: how could he fail to record them specially?
I have heard the admonition that repeated covenants foster disorder, and have sighed that the Great Way could never be restored. Who would have thought that at the beginning of the Spring and Autumn period there would be an instance of understanding reached without a covenant, such as the mutual acknowledgment at Pu? At that time, Duke Xi of Qi sought hegemony in the east, and Duke Xuan of Wei sought hegemony in the north. Although the three-party covenant at Wawu had resolved their grievances, their alignment with opposing parties at the Eastern Gate left their antagonism intact. If a suspicious person had faced this situation, who would not have said that only smearing the lips with sacrificial blood could secure a settlement? Yet the two dukes did otherwise. Wei acknowledged Qi as regional overlord, and the latter already felt assured; Qi acclaimed Wei as a powerful leader, and the former harbored no doubt. Admittedly, their conferring hegemonic status upon one another was not something one would wish to hear of in a flourishing age. Yet, in an age crowded with covenants and oaths, …

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
口血未乾而渝盟者有矣交質子而猶不信者有
矣二公於爭名定伯之際獨一言而喻焉其於有
虞氏未施信而民信夏后氏未施敬而民敬豈相
遠乎春秋特書胥命于蒲非善其事也善其不盟
也荀子以爲春秋善胥命得經意矣又嘗聞善戰
上刑之戒而悲古人之不可作矣孰意春秋之中
亦有不戰而屈如盟于召陵者乎斯時也齊雖欲
伯于北楚亦欲強于南包茅昭王之問桓之義雖
伸方城漢水之對楚之詞且抗使好攻者處此孰
===
不曰必剪此而後食哉而桓公不然退舍以避
之而此之兵不交結盟以禮之而彼之心自服
雖曰愛情而盟亦先王所欲禁然兵爭俶擾之
餘爭地以戰而殺人盈野者有矣爭城以戰而
殺人盈城者有矣桓公於方張難制之楚獨談
笑而麾之其於大舜之舞干苗格文王之因壘
崇降殆庶幾乎春秋特書盟于召陵蓋美其盟
者美其不戰也楊子以爲春秋美召陵知經者
矣吁胥命善焉而後知屢盟之可惡召陵美
punctuated:
口血未乾而渝盟者有矣，交質子而猶不信者有矣。二公於爭名定伯之際，獨一言而喻焉。其於有虞氏未施信而民信、夏后氏未施敬而民敬，豈相遠乎？《春秋》特書「胥命于蒲」，非善其事也，善其不盟也。荀子以爲《春秋》善胥命，得經意矣。
又嘗聞善戰上刑之戒，而悲古人之不可作矣。孰意《春秋》之中，亦有不戰而屈，如盟于召陵者乎？斯時也，齊雖欲伯于北，楚亦欲強于南。包茅、昭王之問，桓之義雖伸；方城、漢水之對，楚之詞且抗。使好攻者處此，孰不曰：「必剪此而後食哉！」而桓公不然，退舍以避之，而此之兵不交；結盟以禮之，而彼之心自服。雖曰愛情而盟，亦先王所欲禁，然兵爭俶擾之餘，爭地以戰而殺人盈野者有矣，爭城以戰而殺人盈城者有矣。桓公於方張難制之楚，獨談笑而麾之。其於大舜之舞干苗格、文王之因壘崇降，殆庶幾乎？《春秋》特書「盟于召陵」，蓋美其盟者，美其不戰也。楊子以爲《春秋》美召陵，知經者矣。吁！胥命善焉，而後知屢盟之可惡；召陵美
translation_en:
…There were those who broke their covenant before the blood on their lips had dried, and those who exchanged sons as hostages yet still did not trust one another. Yet amid their contest for renown and the establishment of hegemony, the two dukes reached an understanding with a single word. How far removed were they from the ruler of Youyu, whose people trusted him before he instituted measures to secure trust, or the ruler of Xia, whose people respected him before he instituted measures to secure respect? In expressly recording that they “mutually acknowledged one another at Pu,” the Spring and Autumn Annals approves not their undertaking itself, but their dispensing with a covenant. Xunzi grasped the Classic’s meaning when he held that the Spring and Autumn Annals approved this mutual acknowledgment.
I have also heard the warning that those skilled in warfare deserve the severest punishment, and have grieved that the men of antiquity cannot rise again. Who would have thought that, amid the events of the Spring and Autumn Annals, there was also a case of securing submission without battle, such as the covenant at Shaoling? At that time, while Qi sought hegemony in the north, Chu likewise sought supremacy in the south. Although Duke Huan asserted the justice of his cause by questioning Chu about its tribute of bundled thatch and the fate of King Zhao, Chu’s reply invoking Fangcheng and the Han River remained defiant. Had someone fond of attacking been in this position, who would not have said, “I must destroy this enemy before I eat!” But Duke Huan acted otherwise. He withdrew his encampment to give way, so that his troops did not engage; he concluded a covenant and treated Chu with ritual courtesy, so that its people submitted of their own accord. Although “making a covenant out of affection” [?] was also something the former kings wished to prohibit, amid the turmoil of armed contention there were those who fought for territory until the slain filled the countryside, and those who fought for cities until the slain filled the cities. Yet Duke Huan, with mere conversation and laughter, brought under his direction Chu, whose power was expanding and was difficult to restrain. Was this not close to the great Shun’s dancing with shields and bringing the Miao to submission, or King Wen’s “relying on ramparts” [?] and bringing about Chong’s surrender? In expressly recording the “covenant at Shaoling,” the Spring and Autumn Annals praises the covenant because it praises the avoidance of battle. Master Yang understood the Classic when he held that the Spring and Autumn Annals praised Shaoling. Ah! Only after recognizing the goodness of the mutual acknowledgment do we understand how hateful repeated covenants are; the excellence of Shaoling…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
焉而後知善戰之可刑春秋經世之書信夫於
戲胥命可善矣不越世而小伯於襄創伯於桓
語王道僖宣其五伯之首亂乎召陵可美矣不
旋踵而志驕於陳業怠於楚語王德桓公其三
王之罪人乎噫其可旣也夫其亦可悲也夫
禮記
三年耕必有一年之食九年耕必有三年
之食
===
同考試官敎諭季批國家之儲蓄當以民食為重
而經文亦自明白作者乃以喪祭平說或又專講喪
祭而民食反不之及殊失輕重之倫此篇理明辭順
深合本旨末復推本於君心可以占于他日之用矣
宜魁多士
劉桂
考試官敎諭劉批得古人制國用廣儲蓄意
考試官學正孫批脫去陳腐自是一機軸
先王之經國歷歲漸久而儲蓄漸廣焉蓋廣儲
蓄經國之首務也使為之不以其漸豈善於經
punctuated:
焉，而後知善戰之可刑。《春秋》，經世之書，信夫！於戲！胥命可善矣，不越世而小伯於襄、創伯於桓。語王道，僖、宣其五伯之首亂乎？召陵可美矣，不旋踵而志驕於陳、業怠於楚。語王德，桓公其三王之罪人乎？噫！其可旣也夫？其亦可悲也夫！
禮記
三年耕，必有一年之食；九年耕，必有三年之食。
同考試官敎諭季批：國家之儲蓄，當以民食為重，而經文亦自明白。作者乃以喪祭平說，或又專講喪祭，而民食反不之及，殊失輕重之倫。此篇理明辭順，深合本旨，末復推本於君心，可以占于他日之用矣。宜魁多士。
劉桂
考試官敎諭劉批：得古人制國用、廣儲蓄意。
考試官學正孫批：脫去陳腐，自是一機軸。
先王之經國，歷歲漸久，而儲蓄漸廣焉。蓋廣儲蓄，經國之首務也。使為之不以其漸，豈善於經
translation_en:
…is praised, and only then do we understand that those skilled in warfare deserve punishment. Truly, the Spring and Autumn Annals is a book for ordering the world! Ah! The mutual agreement merits approval, yet within a single generation a lesser hegemony emerged under Xiang, and hegemony was established under Huan. Judged by the Way of the True King, were not Xi and Xuan the first to initiate the disorder of the Five Hegemons? The covenant at Shaoling merits praise, yet almost immediately Huan’s ambitions grew arrogant toward Chen, and his enterprise grew slack toward Chu. Judged by kingly virtue, was not Duke Huan an offender against the Three Kings? Alas! Can there be an end to this [?]? Is it not also lamentable!
Record of Rites
“Three years of cultivation must yield one year’s food in reserve; nine years of cultivation must yield three years’ food in reserve.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Ji, Instructor: In the state’s accumulation of reserves, the people’s food should take precedence, and the classic’s text itself makes this clear. Yet writers discuss funeral and sacrificial provisions on an equal footing with it; some even discuss funeral and sacrificial provisions exclusively, leaving the people’s food entirely unmentioned. This badly confuses the relative importance of things. This essay’s reasoning is clear and its language fluent, closely according with the passage’s fundamental meaning. At the end it further traces the matter to its root in the ruler’s heart, allowing us to foresee the author’s future usefulness. He deserves to rank first among the candidates.
Liu Gui
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: He grasps the ancients’ intent in regulating state expenditure and enlarging reserves.
Comment by Examiner Sun, Instructor: Free of stale conventions, this has a distinctive approach of its own.
As the former kings administered the state, their reserves gradually increased with the passing years. For enlarging reserves is the foremost task of administering the state. If one undertook this without proceeding gradually, how could one be adept at administering…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
國者哉記王制者謂夫天地之生財有限國家
之用度無窮冢宰之制國用可不廣儲蓄以為
之備耶蓋公家之所有由於耕者之所入故自
一年耕積而至於三年則歷歲既久所入亦多
矣苟以每歲所入用其三而餘其一以三年所
餘之三又已足一歲之用雖或遇夫水旱之災
也吾見有備無患凡民之艱於粒食者于焉發
倉廩以賑貸之使得以遂其仰事俯育之願他
如喪葬祭祀之需有不足言也向使制用無法
===
則旦夕之急且不可救况一歲之間乎耕者之
所獲必為公家之所供故自三年耕積而至於
九年則歷歲滋久所供益多矣苟以每歲所供
餘其一而用其三以九年所餘之九又已周三
年之用雖或遭夫凶荒之變也吾見救荒有策
凡民之苦於饑餒者于焉出穀粟以賙恤之使
得以免夫轉徙流亡之患至於朝聘燕享之資
有不足計也向使費出無經則一歲之艱尚不
能濟况三年之久乎吁自三年之耕積而至於
punctuated: 國者哉？記《王制》者謂夫天地之生財有限，國家之用度無窮，冢宰之制國用，可不廣儲蓄以為之備耶？蓋公家之所有，由於耕者之所入，故自一年耕積而至於三年，則歷歲既久，所入亦多矣。苟以每歲所入，用其三而餘其一，以三年所餘之三，又已足一歲之用。雖或遇夫水旱之災也，吾見有備無患。凡民之艱於粒食者，于焉發倉廩以賑貸之，使得以遂其仰事俯育之願。他如喪葬祭祀之需，有不足言也。向使制用無法，則旦夕之急且不可救，况一歲之間乎？耕者之所獲，必為公家之所供，故自三年耕積而至於九年，則歷歲滋久，所供益多矣。苟以每歲所供，餘其一而用其三，以九年所餘之九，又已周三年之用。雖或遭夫凶荒之變也，吾見救荒有策。凡民之苦於饑餒者，于焉出穀粟以賙恤之，使得以免夫轉徙流亡之患。至於朝聘燕享之資，有不足計也。向使費出無經，則一歲之艱尚不能濟，况三年之久乎？吁！自三年之耕積而至於
translation_en:
…could he be one skilled at governing a state? The author of “Royal Regulations” (Wang zhi) says that the wealth produced by Heaven and Earth is finite, whereas the expenditures of the state are endless. In regulating state expenditure, can the Minister of State fail to enlarge reserves in preparation for these needs? What the public treasury possesses comes from what cultivators bring in. Thus, as cultivation and accumulation extend from one year to three, more years have elapsed and receipts have also grown. If, of each year’s receipts, three portions are used and one retained, the three portions saved over three years will suffice for another year’s expenditure. Even should floods or droughts occur, I see preparedness averting distress. For all those among the people who have difficulty obtaining grain to eat, the granaries can then be opened to provide relief and loans, enabling them to fulfill their wish to support their parents and nourish their children. Other needs, such as funerals, burials, and sacrifices, scarcely require mention. Had expenditure been regulated without proper rules, even an emergency lasting from morning to evening could not have been relieved, much less one lasting a whole year.

What cultivators harvest must supply the public treasury. Thus, as cultivation and accumulation extend from three years to nine, still more years have elapsed and supplies have grown further. If, of each year’s supplies, one portion is retained and three are used, the nine portions saved over nine years will suffice for three years’ expenditure. Even should the calamity of famine occur, I see a means of providing famine relief. For all those among the people who suffer hunger, grain can then be issued to assist them, enabling them to escape the misery of displacement and wandering. As for the resources needed for court audiences, diplomatic visits, and ceremonial banquets, these scarcely require reckoning. Had outlays lacked established rules, even a single year’s hardship could not have been overcome, much less one lasting three years. Ah! From three years of cultivation and accumulation, extending to…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
三十年之通由一年之食推而至於有九年之
蓄先王經國之善孰有加於此哉大抵國以民
爲本民以食爲天論治而先於足食誠萬世之
常道亦夫人之常談也雖晁錯楊炎之流亦能
詳其說以獻於君而況後世老成謀國之士視
錯炎之說何如而有國者每自揺其本自絕於
天何哉用之侈也用之侈心之邪也心正則用
節節則本固天定而天下不足治矣故曰君志
定而天下之治成
===
致禮樂之道舉而錯之天下無難矣
陳銓
同考試官教諭李批樂記題本冠冕類能作之
但不失之冗俗則失之混殽殊無可人意者晚得此卷
乃組織經傳成文不假剽竊而文采燁然是用錄出
考試官教諭劉批說得禮樂感人處明白可取
考試官學正孫批整潔可誦
君子極夫和序之理則致治爲甚易矣蓋禮樂
之道和序而已誠能於此而致其極焉其致治
punctuated:
三十年之通，由一年之食推而至於有九年之蓄，先王經國之善，孰有加於此哉？大抵國以民爲本，民以食爲天，論治而先於足食，誠萬世之常道，亦夫人之常談也。雖晁錯、楊炎之流，亦能詳其說以獻於君，而況後世老成謀國之士，視錯、炎之說何如？而有國者每自揺其本，自絕於天，何哉？用之侈也。用之侈，心之邪也。心正則用節，節則本固天定，而天下不足治矣。故曰：「君志定而天下之治成。」

致禮樂之道，舉而錯之天下，無難矣。

陳銓

同考試官教諭李批：樂記題本冠冕，類能作之，但不失之冗俗，則失之混殽，殊無可人意者。晚得此卷，乃組織經傳成文，不假剽竊，而文采燁然，是用錄出。

考試官教諭劉批：說得禮樂感人處明白，可取。

考試官學正孫批：整潔可誦。

君子極夫和序之理，則致治爲甚易矣。蓋禮樂之道，和序而已。誠能於此而致其極焉，其致治
translation_en:
…an accounting over thirty years, extending from provisions for one year to reserves sufficient for nine years: who could surpass the former kings’ excellence in administering the state? In general, the state takes the people as its foundation, and the people take food as their Heaven. To give priority to sufficient food when discussing government is indeed the enduring Way for all ages, and something everyone commonly says. Even men such as Chao Cuo and Yang Yan could expound this teaching in detail and present it to their rulers. How much more should the seasoned statesmen of later ages be able to do, measured against the teachings of Cuo and Yan? Yet rulers repeatedly shake their own foundation and cut themselves off from Heaven. Why? Because their expenditure is extravagant. Extravagant expenditure arises from a wayward heart. When the heart is upright, expenditure is restrained; with restraint, the foundation is secure and Heaven is settled, and governing the realm requires little effort [?]. Hence the saying: “Once the ruler’s resolve is settled, good government throughout the realm is achieved.”

“Bring the Way of rites and music to its fullest realization, and there will be no difficulty in applying it throughout the realm.”

Chen Quan

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: Topics from the Record of Music are inherently dignified, and most candidates can write on them. Yet their compositions fall either into prolixity and vulgarity or into confusion; scarcely any is pleasing. Late in the process I obtained this script. It weaves the classics and their commentaries into a composition without resorting to plagiarism, and its literary brilliance shines forth. For this reason it has been selected for inclusion.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: The explanation of how rites and music move people is clear and merits approval.

Comment by Examiner Sun, School Instructor: Neat and polished, and worthy of recitation.

When the gentleman fully realizes the principles of harmony and order, bringing about good government becomes very easy. For the Way of rites and music consists simply in harmony and order. If he can truly bring these to their fullest realization, his bringing about good government…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
也豈不易易然哉樂記君子意謂治吾身莫切
於禮樂治天下一本於吾身君子知禮自外作
也故以之治躬使莊敬嚴威之日著而鄙詐易
慢之心無自而入焉知樂由中出也故以之治
心使易直慈良之心生而安乆天神之妙漸造
其極焉禮焉極其順而無斯須之不順則義理
為之外見所謂周旋中禮者是已樂焉極其和
而無斯須之不和則德輝為之內動所謂英華
發外者是已若然則禮樂之道致其極矣吾知
===
至序秩秩而感人之本於我乎具太和洋洋而
動物之機於此乎存舉是禮而錯之天下則蕩
蕩堯封悉囿於合敬之中望容貌而弗敢慢也
推此樂而放諸四海則茫茫禹方咸歸於同愛
之內瞻顏色而弗與爭也不必驅之以刑也而
民之承順者合衆寡而同心捷於風之偃草矣
不必迫之以勢也而民之承聽者合遠近而一
致速於響之應聲矣其於治天下也夫何難哉
吁禮樂之致治其易如此君子可不究心於斯
punctuated: 也，豈不易易然哉？《樂記》君子意謂：治吾身莫切於禮樂，治天下一本於吾身。君子知禮自外作也，故以之治躬，使莊敬嚴威之日著，而鄙詐易慢之心無自而入焉；知樂由中出也，故以之治心，使易直慈良之心生，而安乆天神之妙漸造其極焉。禮焉極其順，而無斯須之不順，則義理為之外見，所謂周旋中禮者是已；樂焉極其和，而無斯須之不和，則德輝為之內動，所謂英華發外者是已。若然，則禮樂之道致其極矣。吾知至序秩秩，而感人之本於我乎具；太和洋洋，而動物之機於此乎存。舉是禮而錯之天下，則蕩蕩堯封悉囿於合敬之中，望容貌而弗敢慢也；推此樂而放諸四海，則茫茫禹方咸歸於同愛之內，瞻顏色而弗與爭也。不必驅之以刑也，而民之承順者合衆寡而同心，捷於風之偃草矣；不必迫之以勢也，而民之承聽者合遠近而一致，速於響之應聲矣。其於治天下也，夫何難哉？吁！禮樂之致治，其易如此，君子可不究心於斯
translation_en: …would it not indeed be exceedingly easy? The meaning of the gentleman discussed in the Record of Music is this: nothing is more essential to governing oneself than ritual and music, and governing the world is rooted entirely in oneself. The gentleman knows that ritual arises from without, and therefore uses it to regulate his conduct, so that solemnity, reverence, dignity, and majesty become daily more manifest, while baseness, deceit, carelessness, and arrogance find no means of entering his heart. He knows that music issues from within, and therefore uses it to govern his heart, so that feelings of ease, uprightness, kindness, and goodness arise, and the subtle efficacy of abiding tranquility and heavenly spirituality [?] gradually reaches its utmost degree. When ritual brings compliance to its utmost degree, with not a moment of noncompliance, moral principle becomes outwardly manifest: this is what is meant by every movement according with ritual. When music brings harmony to its utmost degree, with not a moment of disharmony, the radiance of virtue stirs within: this is what is meant by its finest essence flowering outwardly. If this is so, the Way of ritual and music has been brought to perfection. I know that, with perfect order arrayed in due sequence, the basis for influencing others is fully present in me; with supreme harmony flowing abundantly, the impulse that moves all beings resides here. Take this ritual and establish it throughout the world, and the vast domain of Yao will be wholly encompassed within shared reverence: beholding the gentleman’s bearing, people will not dare to be disrespectful. Extend this music throughout the Four Seas, and the boundless lands of Yu will all come within a common love: beholding his countenance, people will not contend with him. There will be no need to drive them with punishments: the people, obedient and compliant, whether many or few, will unite in purpose more swiftly than grass bends before the wind. There will be no need to compel them with power: the people, heeding and obeying, both far and near, will act as one more swiftly than an echo answers a sound. What difficulty, then, could there be in governing the world? Ah! Such is the ease with which ritual and music bring about good government. Can the gentleman fail to devote his mind to this…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
哉雖然天下不可一日無禮樂尤不可一日無
聖人古之聖人履中正而樂和平故能成雍熈
泰和之治降及後世雜以刑名黄老之術至叔
孫通曹褒之徒出而禮樂之義愈晦焉所以布
於四體興於閨門著於宗廟朝廷者秪見其日
入於紕繆而已故曰不復古禮不變今樂而欲
言治者遠矣或又謂治之隆替不由于此何發
言之易哉
第貳場
===
論
孟子言必稱堯舜
唐愈賢
同考試官訓導禇批以精一之功其機只在吾心便
見堯舜之必可為反覆辯論千餘言皆不出此義而孟子
必稱堯舜之意煥然一新於戯孟子遠矣是論其可少哉
同考試官訓導楊批題極正大士子類能言之然多
蹈襲陳言漫無歸着未見的然有見自肺腑中出者是篇
初讀殊不甚經意徐而尋繹則脉絡貫串意趣無窮說理
punctuated:
哉！雖然，天下不可一日無禮樂，尤不可一日無聖人。古之聖人履中正而樂和平，故能成雍熈泰和之治。降及後世，雜以刑名黄老之術，至叔孫通、曹褒之徒出，而禮樂之義愈晦焉。所以布於四體、興於閨門、著於宗廟朝廷者，秪見其日入於紕繆而已。故曰：「不復古禮，不變今樂，而欲言治者，遠矣。」或又謂治之隆替不由于此，何發言之易哉！

第貳場

論

孟子言必稱堯舜

唐愈賢

同考試官訓導禇批：以精一之功，其機只在吾心，便見堯舜之必可為。反覆辯論千餘言，皆不出此義，而孟子必稱堯舜之意煥然一新。於戯！孟子遠矣，是論其可少哉！

同考試官訓導楊批：題極正大，士子類能言之，然多蹈襲陳言，漫無歸着，未見的然有見、自肺腑中出者。是篇初讀，殊不甚經意，徐而尋繹，則脉絡貫串，意趣無窮。說理
translation_en:
…indeed! Nevertheless, the realm cannot go a single day without rites and music, and still less can it go a single day without a sage. The sages of antiquity practiced centrality and correctness and delighted in peace and harmony; thus they could bring about an age of concord, prosperity, and perfect harmony. In later ages, these were mixed with techniques of administrative accountability and the teachings of Huang-Lao. When men such as Shusun Tong and Cao Bao appeared, the meaning of rites and music became still more obscured. What was expressed through the four limbs, fostered within the household, and manifested in the ancestral temples and at court could only be seen slipping daily further into error. Hence the saying: “Without restoring the ancient rites and changing the music of today, anyone who wishes to speak of good government is far from the mark.” Some even claim that the flourishing or decline of government does not depend on these things. How lightly they speak!

Second Session

Discourse

“Whenever Mencius Spoke, He Invariably Cited Yao and Shun”

Tang Yuxian

Comment by Associate Examiner Chu, Assistant Instructor: Through the work of refinement and single-mindedness, whose pivotal workings lie solely within our own minds, one readily sees that becoming a Yao or a Shun is certainly possible. The essay argues back and forth in more than a thousand characters, never departing from this principle, yet makes the meaning of Mencius’s invariably citing Yao and Shun shine forth anew. Alas! Mencius is far removed from us. Can such a discourse be dispensed with?

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor: The topic is supremely upright and grand. Candidates can generally discuss it, but most repeat worn-out phrases and ramble without reaching a conclusion. One finds no clear insight issuing from their innermost hearts. On first reading this essay, I paid it little attention; on slowly tracing its meaning, however, I found its lines of thought connected throughout and its implications inexhaustible. Writing that expounds principles…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
文字正不貴於一覽而可盡此觀者亦自得之
考試官教諭劉批命題後嘗倣范文正公意自
擬一篇蓋作而後知其不易也況性理文字尤難下手子於
寸晷中出千餘言而無長語中間開闔起伏變化無窮且
意義層出而當時孟子所言門人所不能悉記者如得而
盡聞焉起敬起敬
考試官學正孫批人謂時文無所於用觀此作
直是發明心學宜錄以傳
聖人萬世之師也舍聖人則無所於師君
===
子是以亟稱之也聖人之性吾性也彼能
盡而我乃不能盡夫是以有異耳而其初
則未嘗異也人知其異而忘其初孟子於
是乎有性善之說而徵諸堯舜焉蓋以聖
人而望人人也且堯舜何如人也其知生
知其行安行其盛德崇功振古無加焉夫
人而知之也人不皆聖人也究其一或遺
其二勉於此或仆於彼視諸堯舜之德譬
則天之不可階而升亦夫人而知之也然
punctuated:
文字正不貴於一覽而可盡，此觀者亦自得之。
考試官教諭劉批：命題後，嘗倣范文正公意，自擬一篇。蓋作而後知其不易也，況性理文字尤難下手。子於寸晷中出千餘言，而無長語，中間開闔起伏，變化無窮，且意義層出，而當時孟子所言、門人所不能悉記者，如得而盡聞焉。起敬！起敬！
考試官學正孫批：人謂時文無所於用，觀此作，直是發明心學，宜錄以傳。
聖人，萬世之師也。舍聖人，則無所於師，君子是以亟稱之也。聖人之性，吾性也；彼能盡，而我乃不能盡，夫是以有異耳，而其初則未嘗異也。人知其異而忘其初，孟子於是乎有性善之說，而徵諸堯舜焉，蓋以聖人而望人人也。且堯舜何如人也？其知，生知；其行，安行。其盛德崇功，振古無加焉，夫人而知之也。人不皆聖人也，究其一，或遺其二；勉於此，或仆於彼。視諸堯舜之德，譬則天之不可階而升，亦夫人而知之也。然
translation_en:
…The worth of writing lies precisely in its not being exhaustible at a single glance; readers will discover this for themselves as well.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: After setting the topic, I once followed the idea of Lord Fan Wenzheng and drafted an essay myself. Only after writing it did I realize how difficult it was; writing on human nature and principle is especially hard to begin. Yet in the brief time allotted, you produced more than a thousand words without a superfluous phrase. The unfolding and gathering of the argument, its rises and falls, show endless variation, while layer upon layer of meaning emerges. It is as though we could hear in full what Mengzi said in his day but his disciples could not record completely. My respect is stirred! My respect is stirred!

Comment by Examiner Sun, Instructor: People say that examination prose serves no purpose. Looking at this work, however, one sees that it directly elucidates the learning of the mind. It should be recorded and transmitted.

The sages are the teachers of all ages. Apart from the sages, there is no one to take as a teacher; thus the gentleman repeatedly invokes them. The nature of the sages is my own nature. They can fully realize it, whereas I cannot: this alone accounts for our differences. At the outset, however, there was never any difference. People recognize the differences but forget the original condition. Hence Mengzi advanced his teaching that human nature is good and adduced Yao and Shun as evidence, expecting everyone to become a sage.

Moreover, what sort of men were Yao and Shun? Their knowledge was knowledge possessed from birth; their conduct was conduct practiced with ease. Their abundant virtue and lofty achievements have never been surpassed since antiquity: everyone knows this. Yet not everyone is a sage. In thoroughly pursuing one aspect, a person may neglect another; striving here, one may stumble there. When people look upon the virtue of Yao and Shun, it seems like Heaven, which cannot be reached by climbing a stairway: everyone knows this too. Yet…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
則孟子何為而必稱堯舜也吾知之工言
必稱垂射言必稱羿奕言必稱秋醫言必
稱岐扁師其至也何獨至於士而疑之堯
舜人道之至也吾而非人則已吾亦人也
將非堯舜誰師哉吾之性非堯舜之性歟
吾嘗驗之吾心焉淵乎其神而無方也亦
嘗驗之吾身焉浩乎若化而無累也耳極
天下之聲目極天下之色口極天下之味
鼻極天下之臭形足以盡其然而心足以
===
通其所以然天之與我者本如是全也有
不全者吾身之私蔽之耳而堯舜獨無身
乎哉目之於色也耳之於聲也口之於味
也鼻之於臭也堯舜與人同耳彼惟以身
從心而不以心徇欲故其言曰人心惟危
道心惟微惟精惟一允執厥中是乃堯舜
之所以聖夫聖人之心旣吾同也吾失之
而吾復之其機又無難也則信乎其可為
而孟子之稱之非過也且聲色臭味之交
punctuated: 則孟子何為而必稱堯舜也？吾知之：工言必稱垂，射言必稱羿，奕言必稱秋，醫言必稱岐扁，師其至也。何獨至於士而疑之？堯舜，人道之至也。吾而非人則已，吾亦人也，將非堯舜誰師哉？吾之性非堯舜之性歟？吾嘗驗之吾心焉，淵乎其神而無方也；亦嘗驗之吾身焉，浩乎若化而無累也。耳極天下之聲，目極天下之色，口極天下之味，鼻極天下之臭，形足以盡其然，而心足以通其所以然。天之與我者，本如是全也。有不全者，吾身之私蔽之耳。而堯舜獨無身乎哉？目之於色也，耳之於聲也，口之於味也，鼻之於臭也，堯舜與人同耳。彼惟以身從心，而不以心徇欲，故其言曰：「人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中。」是乃堯舜之所以聖。夫聖人之心旣吾同也，吾失之而吾復之，其機又無難也。則信乎其可為，而孟子之稱之非過也。且聲色臭味之交
translation_en:
…then why must Mengzi always invoke Yao and Shun? I know the reason. In speaking of craftsmanship, one invariably invokes Chui; of archery, Yi; of the game of go, Qiu; and of medicine, Qi Bo and Bian Que: one takes the highest attainment as one’s model. Why doubt this only when it comes to scholars? Yao and Shun represent the highest attainment of the human Way. If I were not human, that would end the matter; but I too am human. Whom, then, should I take as my models if not Yao and Shun? Is my nature not the nature of Yao and Shun?

I have examined this in my own heart-mind: how profound its spiritual efficacy, unrestricted by any fixed form! I have also examined it in my own body: how expansive, as though transforming without encumbrance! The ears encompass all the sounds under Heaven, the eyes all its colors, the mouth all its flavors, and the nose all its smells. The body suffices to apprehend fully how things are, and the heart-mind suffices to comprehend why they are so. What Heaven has bestowed upon me is originally complete in just this way. Wherever it is incomplete, this is merely because the selfishness of my embodied existence obscures it.

But did Yao and Shun alone have no bodies? In the relation of eyes to colors, ears to sounds, mouth to flavors, and nose to smells, Yao and Shun were just like other people. They simply made the body follow the heart-mind, rather than making the heart-mind yield to desires. Thus their words say: “The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. Be discerning, be single-minded, and truly hold fast to the Mean.” This is what made Yao and Shun sages. Since the sages’ heart-mind is the same as mine, if I have lost it and then recover it, the means of doing so present no difficulty. It is therefore indeed credible that one can become like them, and Mengzi’s invocation of them is no exaggeration. Moreover, when sounds, colors, smells, and flavors come into contact…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
於我也有則焉人知其不可過也辨之必
明守之必固存乎心而已矣舉天下之萬
事萬物凡有聲色臭味而接乎吾身者一
聽於心而莫吾蔽焉則天之與我者全矣
天之與我者全而所謂峻德克明玄德升
聞者可幾而及矣孟子之時何時也功利
之私橫流於天下性惡義外之說交鶩而
不可弭自滅其天自棄其身而不復知人
之所以爲人也孟子起而倡言之然後人
===
知天之生人之厚也人之本不異於聖人
也聖人非有能加於吾性之外也然後知
孟子之功與堯舜並而天道賴以立也不
知道者惑焉曰聖賢以是立教云耳而非
其實也夫聖賢者寧有立無實之教以欺
天下後世哉工醫奕射之流必師其所至
士而曰堯舜堯舜云者則笑之以爲狂爲
惑問之則曰堯舜性之也非人力也質柔
則不前氣暗則有蔽嗚呼聖道之不明可
punctuated: 於我也，有則焉。人知其不可過也，辨之必明，守之必固，存乎心而已矣。舉天下之萬事萬物，凡有聲色臭味而接乎吾身者，一聽於心而莫吾蔽焉，則天之與我者全矣。天之與我者全，而所謂峻德克明、玄德升聞者，可幾而及矣。孟子之時何時也？功利之私橫流於天下，性惡義外之說交鶩而不可弭，自滅其天，自棄其身，而不復知人之所以爲人也。孟子起而倡言之，然後人知天之生人之厚也，人之本不異於聖人也，聖人非有能加於吾性之外也。然後知孟子之功與堯舜並，而天道賴以立也。不知道者惑焉，曰：「聖賢以是立教云耳，而非其實也。」夫聖賢者，寧有立無實之教以欺天下後世哉？工醫奕射之流，必師其所至；士而曰「堯舜，堯舜」云者，則笑之以爲狂、爲惑。問之，則曰：「堯舜性之也，非人力也。質柔則不前，氣暗則有蔽。」嗚呼！聖道之不明，可
translation_en:
…as they come into contact with me, there are proper limits. People know that these must not be exceeded. To discern them clearly and hold to them firmly depends solely on the mind. Among all the affairs and things under Heaven, whatever possesses sound, color, smell, or taste and comes into contact with my person must submit entirely to the mind, without obscuring it. Then what Heaven has bestowed upon me will remain whole. With Heaven’s endowment whole, the achievements described as “making lofty virtue shine forth” and “having profound virtue rise to notice” may be approached and attained.

What sort of age was that of Mengzi? Selfish pursuit of achievement and profit swept across the world. The doctrines that human nature is evil and that righteousness is external vied with one another [?] and could not be checked. People extinguished their own heavenly endowment and abandoned themselves, no longer understanding what makes human beings human. Mengzi arose and proclaimed this teaching. Only then did people understand how generously Heaven had endowed human beings at birth, that their fundamental nature did not differ from that of the sages, and that the sages could add nothing beyond the nature we ourselves possess. Only then could they recognize that Mengzi’s achievement ranked alongside those of Yao and Shun, and that the Way of Heaven depended upon it for its establishment.

Those who do not understand the Way are perplexed and say: “The sages and worthies merely used this to establish their teaching; it is not actually true.” But would the sages and worthies ever establish an unfounded teaching to deceive the world and later generations? Craftsmen, physicians, players of the game of go, and archers invariably take as their teachers those who have attained the highest proficiency. Yet when a scholar speaks constantly of “Yao and Shun, Yao and Shun,” they laugh at him as mad and deluded. When questioned, they say: “Yao and Shun possessed this by nature; it was not achieved through human effort. Those whose constitution is weak cannot advance, and those whose vital energy is clouded suffer obstruction.” Alas! That the Way of the sages remains obscure can…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
知矣工醫奕射之流君子不齒今其智乃
反不能及可愧也歟且不精非氣之罪也
吾弗精耳不一非質之罪也吾弗一耳是
故無智無愚無賢無不肖聖道之所在師
之所在也滕世子者嚮道而至烏得弗舉
堯舜而語之然孟子不特為滕世子語也
於曹交則曰堯舜人皆可為也於齊梁諸
君則告以文王之政文王之政亦堯舜之
道也及滕世子之復見不過引成覸諸子
===
之言而終之曰若藥弗瞑眩厥疾弗瘳蓋
作聖之功亦惟致其精與一焉無他術也
欲法堯舜之道盍自求諸心
同前
童承敘
同考試官訓導胡 批 舉業家有言凡論以立意為
先造語次之若立意高遠而遣詞不工未害為佳茍立意不高雖
文如絺繪亦不足觀也已此題場中士子無不知者率皆蹈襲陳
腐牽連隊仗動至三千言殊為可厭此篇以覺字立說脫去
punctuated:
知矣！工醫奕射之流，君子不齒，今其智乃反不能及，可愧也歟！且不精，非氣之罪也，吾弗精耳；不一，非質之罪也，吾弗一耳。是故無智無愚，無賢無不肖，聖道之所在，師之所在也。滕世子者，嚮道而至，烏得弗舉堯舜而語之？然孟子不特為滕世子語也，於曹交則曰：「堯舜，人皆可為也。」於齊梁諸君，則告以文王之政。文王之政，亦堯舜之道也。及滕世子之復見，不過引成覸諸子之言，而終之曰：「若藥弗瞑眩，厥疾弗瘳。」蓋作聖之功，亦惟致其精與一焉，無他術也。欲法堯舜之道，盍自求諸心？

同前
童承敘

同考試官訓導胡批：舉業家有言：「凡論以立意為先，造語次之。若立意高遠而遣詞不工，未害為佳；茍立意不高，雖文如絺繪，亦不足觀也已。」此題場中士子無不知者，率皆蹈襲陳腐，牽連隊仗，動至三千言，殊為可厭。此篇以覺字立說，脫去
translation_en:
…is plain indeed! Gentlemen disdain those who practice crafts, medicine, board games, and archery; yet now their understanding cannot even match that of such people. Is this not shameful? Moreover, failure to attain refinement is no fault of one's vital endowment; it is simply that one has not refined oneself. Failure to attain singleness is no fault of one's native constitution; it is simply that one has not made oneself single-minded. Thus, whether wise or foolish, worthy or unworthy, wherever the Way of the sages resides, there resides one's teacher. The heir apparent of Teng came seeking the Way: how could Mengzi fail to speak to him of Yao and Shun? Yet Mengzi did not speak thus only to the heir apparent of Teng. To Cao Jiao he said, “Anyone can become a Yao or a Shun.” To the rulers of Qi and Liang he spoke of King Wen's government. King Wen's government was also the Way of Yao and Shun. When the heir apparent of Teng came to see him again, he merely quoted the words of Cheng Jian and others, concluding: “If the medicine does not cause dizziness, the illness will not be cured.” The work of becoming a sage consists simply in bringing refinement and singleness to their utmost; there is no other method. If one wishes to emulate the Way of Yao and Shun, why not seek it within one's own heart?

Same as the preceding topic.
Tong Chengxu.

Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Assistant Instructor: Writers on examination composition have said: “In any discourse, establishing the central idea comes first; crafting the language comes second. If the conception is lofty and far-reaching but the wording lacks polish, the piece may still be excellent. If the conception is not lofty, however, even writing as ornate as embroidery and painting is scarcely worth looking at.” There was no candidate in the examination hall unfamiliar with this topic. Almost all repeated stale formulations and strung together stock parallel passages, readily running to three thousand words—truly tiresome. This piece builds its argument around the word ‘awakening’ and casts off…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
陳腐隊仗之言議論層疊而愈出愈奇讀之惟恐終篇如登衡
廬嵩華而睹煙雲突出巖岫間輪困紛縕交生互發令人有日
暮忘歸之趣杜牧之云意勝者詞愈朴而文愈高其是之謂乎
同考試官教諭周批開闔抑揚悉中法度而轉換
過接處血脉聯属不見痕跡盖大手筆也宜髙薦
考試官教諭劉批此篇僅九百字而字字相
應如常山之蛇宜錄之以為冗長者戒
考試官學正孫批蒼老雅健必優於古作者也
君子思有以覺天下而必以聖人望天下
===
天下之不易於覺也久矣而君子思有以
覺之蓋甚不得已也不得已而覺之而顧
以聖人望之不幾於責天下以不可能之
事邪夫天下之事凡彼有而我無者曰不
可能宜也若夫性者天下之所同也而性
之善非一人之私也聖人有之我亦有之
而聖凡異焉者我自異之也因其異而反
諸同則人人皆可以為聖人而天下之迷
者始覺君子所以望於天下者始慰矣孟
punctuated:
陳腐隊仗之言，議論層疊而愈出愈奇，讀之惟恐終篇。如登衡廬嵩華，而睹煙雲突出巖岫間，輪困紛縕，交生互發，令人有日暮忘歸之趣。杜牧之云：「意勝者詞愈朴而文愈高。」其是之謂乎？

同考試官教諭周批：開闔抑揚，悉中法度，而轉換過接處，血脉聯属，不見痕跡，盖大手筆也，宜髙薦。

考試官教諭劉批：此篇僅九百字，而字字相應，如常山之蛇，宜錄之以為冗長者戒。

考試官學正孫批：蒼老雅健，必優於古作者也。

君子思有以覺天下，而必以聖人望天下。

天下之不易於覺也久矣，而君子思有以覺之，蓋甚不得已也。不得已而覺之，而顧以聖人望之，不幾於責天下以不可能之事邪？夫天下之事，凡彼有而我無者，曰不可能，宜也。若夫性者，天下之所同也，而性之善，非一人之私也。聖人有之，我亦有之，而聖凡異焉者，我自異之也。因其異而反諸同，則人人皆可以為聖人，而天下之迷者始覺，君子所以望於天下者始慰矣。孟
translation_en:
…stale expressions and regimented parallelisms. Its arguments build layer upon layer, each more remarkable than the last; one reads it fearing only that it will end. It is like ascending Mounts Heng, Lu, Song, and Hua and seeing mist and clouds suddenly emerge among the crags and peaks, swirling in profusion [?], arising together and unfolding through one another. It gives one the pleasure of forgetting to return home even as evening falls. Du Muzhi said: “When the conception excels, the plainer the wording, the loftier the writing.” Is this not precisely what he meant?

Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: Its opening and closing, restraint and elevation, all conform to the proper rules. At its transitions and connections, the veins of its argument run continuously, leaving no visible traces of joining. This is indeed the work of a masterly writer and merits a high recommendation.

Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: This piece contains only nine hundred characters, yet every character responds to the others, like the snake of Mount Chang. It should be included as a warning to those who write at excessive length.

Examiner Sun, School Instructor, comments: Mature, refined, and vigorous: it surely surpasses the writers of antiquity.

The gentleman seeks a means of awakening all under Heaven, and invariably expects them to become sages.

For a long time, those under Heaven have been difficult to awaken. That the gentleman seeks a means of awakening them is surely because he feels profoundly compelled to do so. Yet if, compelled to awaken them, he nevertheless expects them to become sages, does this not come close to demanding something impossible of everyone under Heaven? In the affairs of the world, when others possess something that I lack, it is reasonable to call it impossible for me. Human nature, however, is shared by everyone under Heaven, and the goodness of that nature is no one person’s private possession. Sages possess it, and I too possess it. If there is a difference between sage and ordinary person, it is I who have made myself different. If, starting from that difference, one returns to what is shared, then everyone can become a sage. Only then will the deluded people under Heaven awaken, and only then will the gentleman’s hopes for all under Heaven be fulfilled. Meng…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
子言必稱堯舜悲哉其覺天下之心也非
獨爲滕世子覺也昔者周道衰聖王不作
邪說橫議譸譸然而鳴於天下者紛如也
楊以爲我墨以兼愛鞅以富彊之術起以
戰衍儀以辯申韓以刑名法術之學貿貿
焉不知吾性爲何物也天下之迷誰其覺
之此孟子之所以悲也間有知人物之有
性者則又擬之杞桼擬之湍水擬之食與
色辭愈繁而理愈晦矣此孟子所以深悲
===
而不容已於言也蓋性者吾之所固有也
渾然而至善也粹然而無惡也喜怒哀樂
之未發也惻隱羞惡辭讓是非之未形也
即書之降衷詩之有則中庸之天命其理
微妙而難言也惟其微妙而難言也故夫
子不言子貢曰夫子之言性與天道不可
得而聞也夫孟子學孔子者也孔子不言
性而孟子諄諄然曰性善性善云者何也
孔子之時楊墨諸家之說未熾也而天下
punctuated:
子言必稱堯舜，悲哉，其覺天下之心也！非獨爲滕世子覺也。昔者周道衰，聖王不作，邪說橫議，譸譸然而鳴於天下者紛如也。楊以爲我，墨以兼愛，鞅以富彊之術，起以戰，衍儀以辯，申韓以刑名法術之學，貿貿焉不知吾性爲何物也。天下之迷，誰其覺之？此孟子之所以悲也。間有知人物之有性者，則又擬之杞桼，擬之湍水，擬之食與色，辭愈繁而理愈晦矣。此孟子所以深悲而不容已於言也。
蓋性者，吾之所固有也，渾然而至善也，粹然而無惡也。喜怒哀樂之未發也，惻隱羞惡辭讓是非之未形也，即《書》之降衷、《詩》之有則、《中庸》之天命，其理微妙而難言也。惟其微妙而難言也，故夫子不言。子貢曰：「夫子之言性與天道，不可得而聞也。」夫孟子學孔子者也，孔子不言性，而孟子諄諄然曰性善、性善云者，何也？孔子之時，楊墨諸家之說未熾也，而天下
translation_en:
…Mencius invariably invoked Yao and Shun when he spoke. How sorrowful was his desire to awaken the world! He sought to awaken not merely the heir apparent of Teng. In former times, when the Way of Zhou declined and no sage king arose, pernicious doctrines and unrestrained arguments clamored throughout the world in bewildering profusion. Yang Zhu advocated acting for oneself; Mo Di, impartial love; Shang Yang, techniques for enriching and strengthening the state; Wu Qi, warfare; Gongsun Yan and Zhang Yi, disputation; and Shen Buhai and Han Fei, the study of forms and names, laws and techniques of rule. In their benightedness, they did not know what our human nature was. Who would awaken the deluded people of the world? This was why Mencius grieved. Occasionally someone recognized that people and other beings possessed a nature, yet would compare it to willow wood [?], to swirling water, or to appetites for food and sex. The more elaborate their words became, the more obscure the principle grew. This was why Mencius grieved so deeply and could not refrain from speaking.
Nature is what we inherently possess: in its wholeness, supremely good; in its purity, free from evil. It is joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure before they arise; compassion, shame and aversion, deference, and the sense of right and wrong before they take form. It is what the Book of Documents calls the bestowal of the moral mean, what the Book of Odes calls the possession of a norm, and what the Doctrine of the Mean calls Heaven’s mandate. Its principle is subtle and difficult to express. Precisely because it is subtle and difficult to express, the Master did not speak of it. Zigong said: “The Master’s words on human nature and the Way of Heaven cannot be heard.” Now Mencius took Confucius as his teacher. Why, then, did Confucius not speak of human nature, while Mencius earnestly repeated, “Human nature is good; human nature is good”? In Confucius’s time, the doctrines of Yang Zhu, Mo Di, and the other schools had not yet flourished, and throughout the world…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之民猶有覺者孟子之時則非孔子之時
矣使孟子亦如孔子之不言則天下之羣
於迷者將無復覺之望此孟子所以不得
不倡明性善之說也然欲倡明是說於天
下而不舉古之能盡其性者以實其言天
下之人將曰是何誑我也欲覺之而反釋
之疑非善覺者也孟子思有以弭其疑而
納諸聖域焉故言必稱乎堯舜且堯舜者
天下皆知其爲大聖人也巍巍蕩蕩夫子
===
===
甞贊之莫不皆以爲不可及也曰不可及
則沮矣沮則怠怠則安於故常而不克自
振抑豈知堯舜無加於我而我不損於堯
舜者乎自孟子之是言出而後天下之沮
於堯舜者始釋君聞之而盡其性焉則戰
國之君亦堯舜之君也民聞之而盡其性
焉則戰國之民亦堯舜之民也孟子以聖
人而望天下之意如此果天下之人皆聖
人焉則楊墨鞅起衍儀申韓之說將誰售
punctuated: 之民猶有覺者。孟子之時，則非孔子之時矣。使孟子亦如孔子之不言，則天下之羣於迷者，將無復覺之望。此孟子所以不得不倡明性善之說也。然欲倡明是說於天下，而不舉古之能盡其性者以實其言，天下之人將曰：「是何誑我也？」欲覺之而反釋之疑，非善覺者也。孟子思有以弭其疑而納諸聖域焉，故言必稱乎堯舜。且堯舜者，天下皆知其爲大聖人也。巍巍蕩蕩，夫子甞贊之，莫不皆以爲不可及也。曰不可及，則沮矣；沮則怠，怠則安於故常而不克自振。抑豈知堯舜無加於我，而我不損於堯舜者乎？自孟子之是言出，而後天下之沮於堯舜者始釋。君聞之而盡其性焉，則戰國之君亦堯舜之君也；民聞之而盡其性焉，則戰國之民亦堯舜之民也。孟子以聖人而望天下之意如此。果天下之人皆聖人焉，則楊墨鞅起衍儀申韓之說將誰售
translation_en: …among the people there were still some who understood. The age of Mengzi, however, was no longer the age of Kongzi. Had Mengzi likewise refrained from speaking, as Kongzi had, the multitudes throughout the realm who were lost in confusion would have had no further hope of awakening. This is why Mengzi could not but proclaim and elucidate the teaching that human nature is good. Yet if he wished to elucidate this teaching throughout the realm without citing ancient men who had fully realized their nature to substantiate his words, people would say, “Why does he deceive us so?” To seek to awaken them but instead leave them in doubt [?] would not be skillful awakening. Mengzi sought a way to dispel their doubts and bring them into the realm of sagehood; hence, whenever he spoke, he invariably invoked Yao and Shun. Everyone under Heaven knew Yao and Shun to be great sages. The Master had praised their towering greatness and boundless grandeur, and everyone considered them beyond reach. To call them beyond reach was to become discouraged; discouragement led to indolence, and indolence to contentment with habitual ways and an inability to rouse oneself. But did people not realize that Yao and Shun possessed nothing beyond what we possess, and that we possess nothing less than Yao and Shun? Only after Mengzi uttered these words did those throughout the realm who were daunted by Yao and Shun begin to overcome their discouragement. If rulers heard this teaching and fully realized their nature, then the rulers of the Warring States would likewise be rulers such as Yao and Shun. If the people heard it and fully realized their nature, then the people of the Warring States would likewise be people such as those of Yao and Shun’s time. Such was Mengzi’s intention in expecting sagehood of everyone under Heaven. If everyone under Heaven indeed became a sage, then to whom could the teachings of Yang Zhu, Mo Di, Shang Yang, Wu Qi, Gongsun Yan, Zhang Yi, Shen Buhai, and Han Fei be peddled…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
乎杞柳湍水食色之論將誰然乎愚於是
知孟子道性善稱堯舜者蓋默寓惓惓望
治之深意也抑嘗求古之善覺者矣有曰
伊尹者以斯道而覺斯民其言曰吾豈若
使是君爲堯舜之君哉吾豈若使是民爲
堯舜之民哉即孟子稱堯舜之意也揚雄
著書十三篇意亦欲覺斯世也其稱舜之
孝禹之功皐陶之謨曰君子絕德是處天
下於不可能之地也是故沮天下爲善之
===
心必自雄言始君子於是見雄之不知性
宜其有善惡混之論也雄論且然無恠乎
後之論性者愈謬也嗚呼猶幸有孟子之
說在也
表
擬宋頒戒石銘于州縣羣臣謝表〔紹興二年〕
李文會
同考試官教諭祜批表體貴典則不貴浮艷貴
punctuated:
乎？杞柳、湍水、食色之論，將誰然乎？愚於是知孟子道性善、稱堯舜者，蓋默寓惓惓望治之深意也。抑嘗求古之善覺者矣，有曰伊尹者，以斯道而覺斯民。其言曰：「吾豈若使是君爲堯舜之君哉？吾豈若使是民爲堯舜之民哉？」即孟子稱堯舜之意也。揚雄著書十三篇，意亦欲覺斯世也。其稱舜之孝、禹之功、皐陶之謨，曰「君子絕德」，是處天下於不可能之地也。是故沮天下爲善之心，必自雄言始。君子於是見雄之不知性，宜其有善惡混之論也。雄論且然，無恠乎後之論性者愈謬也。嗚呼！猶幸有孟子之說在也。
表
擬宋頒戒石銘于州縣羣臣謝表〔紹興二年〕
李文會
同考試官教諭祜批：表體貴典則，不貴浮艷，貴
translation_en:
…? Who, then, would accept the theories likening human nature to willow wood or swirling water, or identifying it with the appetites for food and sex? I thus understand that when Mengzi spoke of the goodness of human nature and praised Yao and Shun, he implicitly conveyed his profound and earnest longing for good government. I have also sought out those of antiquity who excelled at awakening others. There was Yi Yin, who used this Way to awaken the people. He said: “Would it not be better for me to make this ruler a ruler like Yao and Shun? Would it not be better for me to make these people a people like those of Yao and Shun?” This was precisely Mengzi’s intention in praising Yao and Shun.
Yang Xiong wrote a book in thirteen chapters, likewise intending to awaken his age. Yet when he praised Shun’s filial piety, Yu’s achievements, and Gao Yao’s counsels as “the gentleman’s unsurpassable virtue,” he placed everyone in the world in a position where attainment was impossible. Thus, the discouragement of the world’s resolve to do good must have begun with Yang Xiong’s words. From this, the gentleman sees that Yang Xiong did not understand human nature; little wonder that he propounded the theory that goodness and evil are mixed in it. If even Yang Xiong’s account was like this, it is no surprise that later discussions of human nature became increasingly mistaken. Alas! Fortunately, Mengzi’s teaching still survives.
Memorial
A memorial of thanks on behalf of the assembled officials, composed as if upon the Song court’s distribution of the Admonitory Stone Inscription to the prefectures and counties 〔Second year of Shaoxing [1132]〕
Li Wenhui
Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Instructor: “The memorial form prizes classical propriety, not superficial ornament; it prizes …”

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
疏暢不貴艱澁貴莊重不貴纖巧此篇起處闊大而中間鋪敘復
有條理典則疏暢莊重兼有之宜錄之為表式
同考試官教諭張批戒石銘数語凡為守令者觀之
不能不惕然此表自敘感愧之詞甚有動人處良守令讀之未必不
益知勉也
考試官教諭劉批駢儷中含忠愛意起敬起敬
考試官學正孫批得諷諫體
紹興二年六月某日具官臣某等伏蒙
聖恩以贈直龍圖閣臣黃庭堅所書戒石銘頒
===
各州縣令刻石者詢咨四岳虞廷首重黎
元訓迪百官周典申嚴牧伯六條察吏法
舉唐宗八計稽良疏陳陸贄夷攷勵臣之
語何如戒石之銘臣等誠惶誠忭稽首頓
首
上言伏以竹使分符屬專城之保障銅章出
宰寄百里之安危顧茲民命攸司宜我
皇心軫念爰稽古昔肆有箴規宣帝思賢禁諸
郡勿為苛暴漢光圖治飭有司時勸農桑
punctuated:
疏暢，不貴艱澁；貴莊重，不貴纖巧。此篇起處闊大，而中間鋪敘復有條理，典則、疏暢、莊重兼有之，宜錄之為表式。
同考試官教諭張批：戒石銘数語，凡為守令者觀之，不能不惕然。此表自敘感愧之詞，甚有動人處，良守令讀之，未必不益知勉也。
考試官教諭劉批：駢儷中含忠愛意，起敬，起敬！
考試官學正孫批：得諷諫體。
紹興二年六月某日，具官臣某等伏蒙聖恩，以贈直龍圖閣臣黃庭堅所書戒石銘，頒各州縣，令刻石者。
詢咨四岳，虞廷首重黎元；訓迪百官，周典申嚴牧伯。六條察吏，法舉唐宗；八計稽良，疏陳陸贄。夷攷勵臣之語，何如戒石之銘？臣等誠惶誠忭，稽首頓首上言：伏以竹使分符，屬專城之保障；銅章出宰，寄百里之安危。顧茲民命攸司，宜我皇心軫念。爰稽古昔，肆有箴規。宣帝思賢，禁諸郡勿為苛暴；漢光圖治，飭有司時勸農桑。
translation_en:
…free-flowing expression, rather than difficulty and obscurity; dignity, rather than delicate cleverness. This piece opens expansively, while its exposition in the middle is also orderly. It combines classical propriety, fluency, and dignity, and should be recorded as a model memorial.
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: The few words of the Admonitory Stone Inscription cannot fail to awaken vigilance in any prefect or magistrate who reads them. This memorial’s expressions of gratitude and shame are deeply moving in places. Worthy prefects and magistrates who read it may well find further encouragement to exert themselves.
Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: Within its parallel prose lies a spirit of loyalty and devotion. It inspires respect, indeed it does!
Examiner Sun, School Director, comments: It achieves the manner of indirect remonstrance.
On a certain day of the sixth month of the second year of Shaoxing [1132], your servants, so-and-so and others, holding the specified offices, humbly received your sagely grace: the Admonitory Stone Inscription, in the calligraphy of your servant Huang Tingjian, posthumously appointed Attendant of the Longtu Pavilion, was distributed to every prefecture and county with orders that it be engraved in stone.
In consulting the Four Mountain Chiefs, the court of Yu placed the common people foremost; in instructing the hundred officials, the institutions of Zhou reiterated strict requirements for regional governors. A Tang emperor instituted six provisions for scrutinizing officials; Lu Zhi presented a memorial setting out eight criteria for assessing worthy men. Upon impartially examining these words of encouragement to ministers, how do they compare with the Admonitory Stone Inscription? Your servants, truly fearful and truly joyful, bow their heads to the ground and submit this memorial:
We humbly consider that those entrusted with the bamboo tallies of office bear responsibility for protecting the cities under their sole charge; those who go forth as magistrates with bronze seals are entrusted with the security or peril of districts a hundred li across. Since the people’s lives depend upon these officials, it is fitting that our sovereign should hold them in his compassionate concern. Thus, examining the precedents of antiquity, you have issued admonitions and rules. Emperor Xuan, seeking worthy men, forbade the commanderies to act harshly and violently; Emperor Guangwu of Han, striving for good government, instructed the responsible officials to encourage farming and sericulture at the proper seasons…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
心雖切于閭閻言未登諸碑碣欽承異賚
喜溢同官善哉經世之言美矣名臣之筆
瞻宸稽首莊誦盤盂涓日命工敬礱琬琰
大書深刻期永久以無磨蚤視暮瞻儼神
明之有鑒茲蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
聖學自天
神謨振古
求言罪己配三王二帝之明
===
立政任人弘
一祖五宗之制還元祐黨人之爵而士氣伸表
靖康伏節之臣而人心悅慮求才不廣復
賢良方正之科謂取士無方定詩賦經義
之法
殿廷延老靡倦咨諏
宵旰憂民尤先郡邑鄙嶧山之刻石虛侈秦
功陋泗水之鐫銘徒張漢烈燕然數語事
媿於詞桐栢遺碑贊浮其實觀黃氏四言
punctuated: 心雖切于閭閻，言未登諸碑碣。欽承異賚，喜溢同官。善哉，經世之言！美矣，名臣之筆！瞻宸稽首，莊誦盤盂；涓日命工，敬礱琬琰。大書深刻，期永久以無磨；蚤視暮瞻，儼神明之有鑒。茲蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，聖學自天，神謨振古。求言罪己，配三王二帝之明；立政任人，弘一祖五宗之制。還元祐黨人之爵，而士氣伸；表靖康伏節之臣，而人心悅。慮求才不廣，復賢良方正之科；謂取士無方，定詩賦經義之法。殿廷延老，靡倦咨諏；宵旰憂民，尤先郡邑。鄙嶧山之刻石，虛侈秦功；陋泗水之鐫銘，徒張漢烈。燕然數語，事媿於詞；桐栢遺碑，贊浮其實。觀黃氏四言
translation_en:
…Though their concern for the common people was earnest, their words had not been inscribed on stone monuments. Reverently receiving this extraordinary gift, we and our fellow officials overflow with joy. Excellent indeed are these words for governing the world! Beautiful indeed is the writing of this renowned minister! Facing the imperial presence, we bow our heads to the ground and solemnly recite these admonitions, like those inscribed on basins and bowls. Choosing an auspicious day, we commission craftsmen reverently to polish the fine stone. We have the words written large and carved deep, hoping that they will endure forever without wearing away. Viewing them morning and evening, we feel as though divine powers were watching over us.
This is because we have humbly had the good fortune to encounter Your Majesty, 〇〇〇〇, whose sagely learning is Heaven-endowed and whose divine counsels surpass antiquity. In soliciting advice and acknowledging your own faults, you match the wisdom of the Three Kings and Two Emperors; in establishing government and appointing men, you extend the institutions of the one founding ancestor and five ancestral emperors. You restored the noble titles of the Yuanyou partisans, and the spirits of scholars rose; you honored the ministers who died steadfast in loyalty during the Jingkang era, and the people's hearts rejoiced. Concerned that the search for talent was insufficiently broad, you restored the examination category for the Worthy and Good, Upright and Honest. Holding that the selection of scholars lacked proper methods, you established regulations for poetry and rhapsodies and for exposition of the Classics. You invite elders into the palace court and consult them tirelessly. Rising early and eating late in your concern for the people, you give particular priority to prefectures and counties.
You disdain the stone inscription at Yishan, which vainly magnifies Qin's achievements, and scorn the inscription at Sishui, which merely exaggerates Han's glorious deeds. In the few lines commemorating Yanran, the deeds fall shamefully short of the wording; on the surviving stele at Tongbai, the praise exceeds the facts. When we examine Master Huang's text in four-character lines…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之帖類揚子百官之箴頒諸邇遐昭乎鑒
戒臣等銜叨守令政拙催科荷
聖主之優慈濫隨五馬幸銓曹之俯錄浪擬雙
鳧自虞斧鉞焉迯詎意銘辭之及闔門食
禄飽逮妻孥終嵗安居坐充賓祭兩岐莫
頌舉匕箸以增慙五袴無謠顧釜鍾而重
懼昭昭上帝居高而聽卑蠢蠢下民好仁
而惡虐維斯片石若彼嚴師觸目警心不
必酌泉而知勵諦觀熟誦終期載石以見
===
廉摩挲感厥丹衷摹塌傳乎墨本自兹以
往益殫乃心雖無來暮之歌尚勉去思之
愛不貪為寶敢植園葵惟儉是圖何羞布
被魚懸虎避仰懷循吏之高風三畏四知
寤寐古人之盛事素餐可耻寧忘君子之
譏樂土爰懷永鑒魏風之刺誓保民若赤
子願守俸如井泉伏望
顧畏民畧
克謹天戒內脩外攘邁宣王恢復之功雪耻
punctuated: 之帖，類揚子《百官之箴》，頒諸邇遐，昭乎鑒戒。臣等銜叨守令，政拙催科，荷聖主之優慈，濫隨五馬；幸銓曹之俯錄，浪擬雙鳧。自虞斧鉞焉迯，詎意銘辭之及！闔門食禄，飽逮妻孥；終嵗安居，坐充賓祭。兩岐莫頌，舉匕箸以增慙；五袴無謠，顧釜鍾而重懼。昭昭上帝，居高而聽卑；蠢蠢下民，好仁而惡虐。維斯片石，若彼嚴師，觸目警心，不必酌泉而知勵；諦觀熟誦，終期載石以見廉。摩挲感厥丹衷，摹塌傳乎墨本。自兹以往，益殫乃心。雖無來暮之歌，尚勉去思之愛。不貪為寶，敢植園葵？惟儉是圖，何羞布被？魚懸虎避，仰懷循吏之高風；三畏四知，寤寐古人之盛事。素餐可耻，寧忘君子之譏？樂土爰懷，永鑒《魏風》之刺。誓保民若赤子，願守俸如井泉。伏望顧畏民畧，克謹天戒，內脩外攘，邁宣王恢復之功，雪耻
translation_en:
…the inscribed text resembles Master Yang’s Admonitions to the Hundred Officials. Distributed far and near, it clearly provides a lesson and a warning. We, your servants, unworthily hold office as prefects and magistrates, inept in government and the collection of taxes. Through the sagely sovereign’s abundant kindness, we have undeservedly joined the ranks of those who ride in five-horse carriages; fortunately noticed by the Ministry of Personnel, we presumptuously compare ourselves to the magistrate whose shoes became a pair of wild ducks. We ourselves feared that we could not escape the executioner’s axe; how could we have expected to receive the words of this inscription!

Our entire households subsist on official salaries, whose bounty feeds even our wives and children. We live at ease throughout the year, with our needs for receiving guests and offering sacrifices supplied without exertion. No one praises us for grain bearing double ears; lifting our spoons and chopsticks, we feel still greater shame. No songs celebrate our provision of five pairs of trousers; looking at our measures of grain, we feel renewed dread. The luminous Lord on High dwells aloft yet hears those below; the teeming common people love benevolence and hate oppression. This single stone is like a stern teacher: whenever it catches the eye, it admonishes the heart. We need not drink from the spring to know that we must exert ourselves. Gazing attentively and reciting its words until familiar, we hope ultimately to demonstrate our integrity by carrying away only a stone. These allusions recall officials who upheld their integrity at the ‘Spring of Greed’ and whose departing baggage contained only a stone for ballast. As we stroke the inscription, we are moved by the sincere devotion it expresses; we reproduce it in ink rubbings for circulation.

From this time forward, we shall devote our hearts still more fully to our duties. Though there may be no songs lamenting that we came so late, we shall strive to earn the affection that makes people remember an official after his departure. Taking freedom from greed as our treasure, would we dare plant mallows in our gardens and compete with the people for profit? Seeking frugality alone, why should we be ashamed of a cloth coverlet? The fish hung up and the tigers that fled recall the lofty conduct of exemplary officials, which we revere. The three objects of awe and the four witnesses to a secret deed recall the great deeds of the ancients, which occupy our thoughts waking and sleeping. To eat without earning one’s keep is shameful: how could we forget the gentleman’s reproach? Cherishing the prospect of a happy land, we shall always take warning from the satire in the Airs of Wei. We vow to protect the people as newborn children and wish to preserve our official stipends as carefully as a wellspring.

We humbly hope that Your Majesty will regard with awe the people’s concerns [?], faithfully heed Heaven’s warnings, cultivate good government within and repel threats without, surpass King Xuan’s achievement in restoring his realm, and wipe away humiliation…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
除光跨光武中興之業紀豐功於磨崖之
石納直諫爲丹扆之箴
澤沛廟堂
慶延州縣臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞臣等誠懽誠忭稽首頓首謹言
===
第叁塲
策
第一問
唐愈賢
同考試官訓導褚批塲中士子於
皇祖神功處類能言之至於
聖德之實茫乎不知所謂亦如萬物荷天地生成之德而不知元氣運行之所以
然也此篇獨能言之而末復寓規諷之意盖不必試以職
司而其忠
punctuated:
除光，跨光武中興之業，紀豐功於磨崖之石，納直諫爲丹扆之箴。澤沛廟堂，慶延州縣。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。臣等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首，謹言。
第叁塲
策
第一問
唐愈賢
同考試官訓導褚批：塲中士子於皇祖神功處，類能言之；至於聖德之實，茫乎不知所謂。亦如萬物荷天地生成之德，而不知元氣運行之所以然也。此篇獨能言之，而末復寓規諷之意。盖不必試以職司，而其忠
translation_en:
…remove [“radiance,” unclear in the transcription] [?], and surpass Emperor Guangwu’s achievement in restoring the dynasty. Record your great accomplishments in an inscription carved into a cliff, and accept forthright remonstrance as an admonition beside the vermilion imperial screen. May your beneficence flow abundantly through the court, and your blessings extend to the prefectures and counties. We, your servants, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Sagely Majesty with the utmost fervor and trembling reverence. We respectfully submit this memorial to convey our thanks. With heartfelt joy and gladness, we bow our heads to the ground and repeatedly kowtow, respectfully presenting these words.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Tang Yuxian
Comment by Associate Examiner Chu, Assistant Instructor: Candidates in the examination generally can discuss the august imperial ancestor’s divine achievements; when it comes to the substance of his sagely virtue, however, they are utterly at a loss to explain it. They resemble the myriad things, which receive Heaven and Earth’s beneficence in bringing them into being and nurturing them, yet do not understand how primordial vital energy operates. This essay alone succeeds in explaining it, and its conclusion also conveys an intent to admonish through indirect remonstrance. Indeed, there is no need to test its author in an official post to discern his loyalty…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
君愛
國之心可覘知矣賢科首薦宜哉
同考試官訓導楊批脩德法
祖以保其成功此正
今日急務子能言之切當且詞温意婉有章疏體告君者不當如是邪
考試官教諭劉批說法
祖處忠愛藹然讀之令人斂袵
考試官學正孫批詳而整
作於前而建神功者必本之聖德繼於後
而脩聖德者斯保乎神功夫德者功之本
功者德之發德之大者功之大也顧作之
者匪功不垂而繼之者惟慎脩厥德焉爾
矣故曰創業固難守成不易然則不世之
神功建於我
皇祖者固本諸非常之
聖德而
今日欲保其神功以衍億萬年無疆之休者豈
有出於脩德之外者乎今夫聖人之道蘊
punctuated:
君愛國之心可覘知矣。賢科首薦，宜哉！

同考試官訓導楊批：脩德法祖，以保其成功，此正今日急務。子能言之切當，且詞温意婉，有章疏體，告君者不當如是邪？

考試官教諭劉批：說法祖處，忠愛藹然，讀之令人斂袵。

考試官學正孫批：詳而整。

作於前而建神功者，必本之聖德；繼於後而脩聖德者，斯保乎神功。夫德者，功之本；功者，德之發。德之大者，功之大也。顧作之者匪功不垂，而繼之者惟慎脩厥德焉爾矣。故曰：「創業固難，守成不易。」然則不世之神功建於我皇祖者，固本諸非常之聖德；而今日欲保其神功，以衍億萬年無疆之休者，豈有出於脩德之外者乎？今夫聖人之道，蘊
translation_en:
…his heart, loyal to his ruler and loving toward his country, can be discerned. How fitting that Yuxian should be recommended first in this examination!

Comment by Associate Examiner Yang, Assistant Instructor: Cultivating virtue and emulating the imperial ancestor to preserve his achievements—this is precisely the urgent task of the present day. You address it aptly and pointedly; moreover, your language is gentle and your meaning tactfully expressed, in the manner of a memorial to the throne. Should not those who counsel the ruler do so in just this way?

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: In the passage discussing emulation of the imperial ancestor, loyalty and devotion shine forth. Reading it makes one straighten one's robes in respect.

Comment by Examiner Sun, Instructor: Detailed and well ordered.

He who first establishes a foundation and accomplishes wondrous deeds must ground them in sagely virtue; he who succeeds him and cultivates sagely virtue thereby preserves those wondrous achievements. Virtue is the root of achievement; achievement is the manifestation of virtue. Great virtue produces great achievement. Yet the founder can leave no enduring legacy without achievement, while his successor need only cultivate his virtue with care. Thus it is said: “Founding an enterprise is indeed difficult; preserving its accomplishments is not easy.” The wondrous achievements of our imperial ancestor, rarely equaled across the ages, were assuredly rooted in extraordinary sagely virtue. If today we wish to preserve those achievements and extend their boundless blessings for countless millions of years, can there be any means beyond cultivating virtue? Now, as for the Way of the sage, held within…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之爲德行行之爲事業而況大君之任至
重也開基之主尤難也使非有配天地之
聖德極參賛之神功其何以肇鴻基而垂
大統哉昔者吾夫子繋易之爻而見諸十
三卦者如羲農黄帝之開物成務制器利
用渾渾乎無以尚矣序書斷自唐虞而載
之二典者如堯舜之俊德重華治曆明時
蕩蕩乎無能名矣後五帝而傳世久遠者
爲夏商周始受命則大禹成湯武王也語
===
其功則地平天成兆民允殖四海永清固
無以異矣語其德則文命四敷懋昭大德
惇信明義皆聖人也而孟子以爲堯舜性
之湯武反之焉然禹固無愧於堯舜而湯
武及其成功則一豈有異乎哉其爲之賛
襄者若稷播百穀契敷五教阿衡格天之
勳尚父鷹揚之烈皆一時之聖賢也後三
代而享國長久者爲漢唐宋始創業則高
祖文皇藝祖也語其功則誅秦之暴除隋
punctuated: 之爲德行，行之爲事業。而況大君之任至重也，開基之主尤難也。使非有配天地之聖德、極參賛之神功，其何以肇鴻基而垂大統哉？昔者吾夫子繋易之爻，而見諸十三卦者，如羲農黄帝之開物成務、制器利用，渾渾乎無以尚矣。序書斷自唐虞，而載之二典者，如堯舜之俊德重華、治曆明時，蕩蕩乎無能名矣。後五帝而傳世久遠者爲夏商周，始受命則大禹、成湯、武王也。語其功，則地平天成、兆民允殖、四海永清，固無以異矣；語其德，則文命四敷、懋昭大德、惇信明義，皆聖人也。而孟子以爲堯舜性之，湯武反之焉。然禹固無愧於堯舜，而湯武及其成功則一，豈有異乎哉？其爲之賛襄者，若稷播百穀、契敷五教、阿衡格天之勳、尚父鷹揚之烈，皆一時之聖賢也。後三代而享國長久者爲漢唐宋，始創業則高祖、文皇、藝祖也。語其功，則誅秦之暴、除隋
translation_en:
… becomes virtuous conduct; put into practice, it becomes achievement. How much more is this so when the sovereign’s charge is supremely weighty, and the task of a ruler founding a dynasty especially difficult! Without sagely virtue matching Heaven and Earth, and divine accomplishments fully assisting their transforming work, how could he establish a magnificent foundation and transmit the great imperial succession?

In antiquity, our Master Confucius appended explanations to the lines of the Book of Changes. What is revealed in its thirteen hexagrams—the achievements of Fuxi, Shennong, and the Yellow Emperor in making things available and bringing undertakings to completion, fashioning implements and facilitating their use—was so comprehensive that nothing could surpass it. In arranging the Book of Documents, he began with Tang and Yu. What is recorded in its two Canons—the eminent virtue of Yao and the renewed splendor of Shun, their ordering of the calendar and clarification of the seasons—was so vast that words could not describe it.

After the Five Emperors, the dynasties that endured through many generations were Xia, Shang, and Zhou. Those who first received the Mandate were Yu the Great, Cheng Tang, and King Wu. Speaking of their achievements, the land was brought to order and Heaven’s work completed; the multitude of the people truly flourished; and all within the Four Seas enjoyed lasting peace. In these respects there was certainly no difference among them. Speaking of their virtue, cultivated instruction spread to the four quarters; great virtue was gloriously manifested; and trustworthiness was upheld and righteousness made clear. All were sages. Yet Mencius held that Yao and Shun possessed these qualities by nature, whereas Tang and Wu returned to them through cultivation. Nevertheless, Yu was certainly worthy of comparison with Yao and Shun; and when Tang and Wu attained their achievements, the result was the same. How could there be any difference?

Those who assisted them—Ji, who sowed the hundred grains; Xie, who disseminated the five teachings; Aheng, whose meritorious service reached Heaven; and Shangfu, whose martial prowess soared like an eagle—were all sages and worthies of their age.

After the Three Dynasties, those that enjoyed long possession of the realm were Han, Tang, and Song. Their founding rulers were Gaozu, Emperor Wen, and Yizu. Speaking of their achievements, they punished Qin’s tyranny and eliminated Sui’s …

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
之亂較之取天下於幼主者不無優劣矣
語其德則豁達大度畏義好賢寬仁多恕
皆賢君也而史臣以為天資偶合事多假
仁焉然漢有大綱宋有家法較之閨門聚
麀禁庭蹀血者亦豈無優劣哉其為之輔
佐者若良何之元功房杜之相業普有仁
者之功彬有不伐之美皆一時之勳舊也
於戲三代風遐世不聞純王之治久矣胡
元竊命汙我中華三綱既淪九法盡斁蓋
===
自開闢以來未有之亂也我
皇祖龍飛淮甸汛掃腥羶盡收諸夏之境土大
明天命之彛倫則自生民以來未有之功
也使不有非常之德抑何所本邪然如天
之德莫可名狀愚也叨被覆載之下伏讀
聖製相傳父老蓋甞竊窺其一二矣觀論道而
本乎執中論治而主乎堯舜孝先有哀感
之誠遇災有脩德之諭悟庶徵之應則洪
範為之親註得大學之傳則衍義書於兩
punctuated:
之亂，較之取天下於幼主者，不無優劣矣。語其德，則豁達大度、畏義好賢、寬仁多恕，皆賢君也。而史臣以為天資偶合，事多假仁焉。然漢有大綱，宋有家法，較之閨門聚麀、禁庭蹀血者，亦豈無優劣哉？其為之輔佐者，若良何之元功、房杜之相業、普有仁者之功、彬有不伐之美，皆一時之勳舊也。
於戲！三代風遐，世不聞純王之治久矣。胡元竊命，汙我中華，三綱既淪，九法盡斁，蓋自開闢以來未有之亂也。我皇祖龍飛淮甸，汛掃腥羶，盡收諸夏之境土，大明天命之彛倫，則自生民以來未有之功也。使不有非常之德，抑何所本邪？然如天之德，莫可名狀。愚也叨被覆載之下，伏讀聖製，相傳父老，蓋甞竊窺其一二矣。觀論道而本乎執中，論治而主乎堯舜，孝先有哀感之誠，遇災有脩德之諭，悟庶徵之應，則《洪範》為之親註；得《大學》之傳，則《衍義》書於兩
translation_en:
…the disorder of the Sui: compared with taking the realm from a child ruler, these achievements were not without distinctions of superiority and inferiority. As for their virtues—open-mindedness and magnanimity, reverence for righteousness and esteem for worthy men, generosity and abundant forbearance—they were all worthy rulers. Yet the historians considered their natural dispositions only coincidentally consonant with virtue, and held that their actions often merely assumed the guise of benevolence. Nevertheless, the Han possessed its broad governing principles, and the Song its dynastic rules. Compared with those whose inner chambers resembled deer sharing mates and whose palace courts were awash with blood, were there not also distinctions of superiority and inferiority? Among those who assisted them were Zhang Liang and Xiao He, with their founding achievements; Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui, with their accomplishments as chief ministers; Zhao Pu, with achievements befitting a benevolent man; and Cao Bin, with the virtue of never boasting of his merits. All were veteran servants of distinguished achievement in their day.
Alas! The ways of the Three Dynasties are far distant; it has long been since the world heard of government wholly according to the kingly Way. The barbarian Yuan usurped Heaven’s mandate and defiled our central realm. The Three Bonds collapsed, and the nine governing norms were utterly corrupted. Such disorder had never existed since the world first opened. Our imperial ancestor rose like a dragon in the Huai region, swept away the rank and foul, recovered all the territories of the Chinese lands, and brilliantly clarified the enduring human relationships ordained by Heaven. Such achievement had never existed since humankind began. Had he not possessed extraordinary virtue, upon what could it have rested? Yet his virtue, like Heaven itself, cannot be named or described. Unworthy as I am, I have enjoyed his sheltering and sustaining beneficence. Reverently reading his imperial writings and the accounts passed down by the elders, I have ventured to glimpse something of it. I observe that, in discussing the Way, he grounded it in holding fast to the Mean; in discussing government, he took Yao and Shun as his guides. In filial devotion to his forebears, he showed a sincerity of grief that moved others; when disasters occurred, he issued instructions to cultivate virtue. Understanding how the various natural signs corresponded to human conduct, he personally annotated the Great Plan. Having grasped the transmitted teaching of the Great Learning, he had the Extended Meaning inscribed in the two …

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
廡
聖政有精誠之錄
祖訓有典則之貽豈不足以匹休三代聖王之
德而陋漢唐宋諸君於下風也哉當時佐
命元臣文如沉幾先物稱為子房之劉基
論思納誨稱為純臣之宋濂武如伐狄陰
山雪耻千古之徐達席卷吳漢功如敬德
之常遇春其所以翊賛
皇猷於海宇昭布人文於
===
黼扆者豈非
聖祖之良股肱哉今
皇上嗣大曆服勵精圖治執事以為脩德建功
宜無出於法祖之外者固也愚則曰繼非
常之德者保不世之功者也何也普天之
下莫非王土今日之土宇
聖祖之土宇也率土之濱莫非王臣今日之人
民
聖祖之人民也雖使五帝更生三王復作尚何
punctuated:
廡。聖政有精誠之錄，祖訓有典則之貽，豈不足以匹休三代聖王之德，而陋漢唐宋諸君於下風也哉？當時佐命元臣，文如沉幾先物、稱為子房之劉基，論思納誨、稱為純臣之宋濂；武如伐狄陰山、雪耻千古之徐達，席卷吳漢、功如敬德之常遇春。其所以翊賛皇猷於海宇、昭布人文於黼扆者，豈非聖祖之良股肱哉？
今皇上嗣大曆服，勵精圖治。執事以為脩德建功，宜無出於法祖之外者，固也。愚則曰：「繼非常之德者，保不世之功者也。」何也？普天之下，莫非王土，今日之土宇，聖祖之土宇也；率土之濱，莫非王臣，今日之人民，聖祖之人民也。雖使五帝更生，三王復作，尚何
translation_en:
…side galleries. His sagely governance is recorded in the Record of Perfect Sincerity, and his Ancestral Instructions bequeath authoritative standards. Is this not sufficient to rival the virtue of the sage kings of the Three Dynasties and leave the rulers of Han, Tang, and Song far beneath him? Among the chief ministers who assisted the establishment of his rule were civil officials such as Liu Ji, whose profound discernment anticipated events and who was acclaimed as another Zifang, and Song Lian, who deliberated on affairs and offered counsel, and was acclaimed as a minister of pure integrity. Among the military commanders were Xu Da, who attacked the northern peoples at Yinshan and wiped away the humiliation of ages, and Chang Yuchun, who swept away Wu and Han, with achievements comparable to Jingde’s. In assisting the imperial plans throughout the realm and bringing the civil virtues into brilliant expression before the throne, were they not the Sage Ancestor’s worthy arms and legs?
Now His Majesty has succeeded to the great imperial mandate and devotes his energies to good government. You maintain that cultivating virtue and establishing achievements should proceed entirely through emulating the ancestor; this is certainly so. Yet I would say: “To carry forward extraordinary virtue is to preserve achievements unparalleled in the ages.” Why? Beneath all Heaven, there is no land that is not the king’s: the territory of today is the Sage Ancestor’s territory. To the furthest shores of the land, there are none who are not the king’s subjects: the people of today are the Sage Ancestor’s people. Even if the Five Emperors were born again and the Three Kings returned, what further…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
功業之可建邪然則
宵旰孶孶圖惟繼述者宜何如哉必也敬
天而勤民必也親賢而遠奸必也謹
慈宮之奉必也嚴
郊廟之祭必也節游觀而窒嗜慾必也開言路
而重爵賞則
洪武之治復見於今日而彌光
寶曆之傳遠及于億萬年而益固矣芻蕘之
見如此廟堂密勿必有至論儻採而獻之
===
則涓埃之微未必無海岳萬一之助也
第二問
童承敘
同考試官訓導胡批性理之學本自難言此策問
道統相傳同異處非潜心玩理之士其何以措辭即使措辭華
贍而不中肯綮亦徒辭也是篇折論群聖禮義之旨而會之
於一中之說不蔓不枝不浮不強其聞濂洛緒論而有會於
心者邪
同考試官教諭周批廉耻不得抗禮義而為四維
punctuated:
功業之可建邪？然則，宵旰孶孶圖惟繼述者，宜何如哉？必也敬天而勤民，必也親賢而遠奸，必也謹慈宮之奉，必也嚴郊廟之祭，必也節游觀而窒嗜慾，必也開言路而重爵賞，則洪武之治復見於今日而彌光，寶曆之傳遠及于億萬年而益固矣。芻蕘之見如此，廟堂密勿，必有至論，儻採而獻之，則涓埃之微，未必無海岳萬一之助也。
第二問
童承敘
同考試官訓導胡批：性理之學，本自難言。此策問道統相傳同異處，非潜心玩理之士，其何以措辭？即使措辭華贍而不中肯綮，亦徒辭也。是篇折論群聖禮義之旨，而會之於一中之說，不蔓不枝，不浮不強，其聞濂洛緒論而有會於心者邪？
同考試官教諭周批：廉耻不得抗禮義而為四維。
translation_en:
