…what achievements could there be left to establish? How, then, should His Majesty proceed as he diligently plans, from before dawn until late at night, to carry on his ancestors’ work? He must revere Heaven and attend diligently to the people; draw close to the worthy and keep the wicked at a distance; serve the Empress Dowager with care; solemnly conduct the sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temples; restrain excursions and sightseeing and curb appetites and desires; open channels for remonstrance and give due weight to the bestowal of ranks and rewards. Then the good government of the Hongwu era will appear again today with still greater brilliance, and the transmission of the imperial succession will extend through countless ages with ever greater security. Such are the views of this humble woodcutter. Those who labor diligently at court surely have the most judicious counsel. If they should adopt these views and present them to the throne, even something as slight as a drop of water or a speck of dust might contribute some infinitesimal assistance to an ocean or a mountain.
Second Question
Tong Chengxu
Comment by Associate Examiner Hu, Assistant Instructor: The study of human nature and principle is inherently difficult to discuss. This policy question asks about similarities and differences in the transmission of the succession of the Way. How could anyone who has not devoted himself to pondering principle find words to address it? Even if his language were ornate and copious, it would be mere verbiage if it failed to reach the heart of the matter. This essay analyzes the purport of ritual propriety and righteousness as taught by the various sages and brings their teachings together in the doctrine of the single Mean. It neither sprawls nor branches off; it is neither superficial nor strained. Can its author be someone who has heard the inherited teachings of the Lian and Luo schools and grasped them in his heart?
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor: Integrity and a sense of shame cannot be ranked alongside ritual propriety and righteousness to constitute the Four Bonds…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
柳子厚嘗有是論此篇發明痛快足破群疑子厚復作必
以予爲知言哉
考試官教諭劉批禮義策如此答者絕少
考試官學正孫批是析理文字
善論道統之傳者不徒于其言而必于其
心夫道原於天而具于人心心之同者道
之同也群聖之言無非所以明道然有互
相發明者言雖不同道則未始有異也苟
徒于其言而不于其心何足以論一中之
===
妙於千古之上乎愚未聞道也道統之傳
不敢妄議請因執事之問而言之禮者天
理之節文義者人心之裁制配乎天則爲
亨爲利而分四時屬乎人則合仁與智而
爲四德若夫有分辨之廉有羞惡之耻固
非出乎禮義之外也故人有禮義者必有
廉耻無廉耻者必無禮義則廉耻者誠禮
義中之一事大德中之小節耳舉禮義並
仁智而稱四德可也推廉耻抗禮義而稱
punctuated:
柳子厚嘗有是論，此篇發明痛快，足破群疑。子厚復作，必以予爲知言哉！

考試官教諭劉批：禮義策如此答者絕少。

考試官學正孫批：是析理文字。

善論道統之傳者，不徒于其言，而必于其心。夫道原於天，而具于人心，心之同者，道之同也。群聖之言，無非所以明道，然有互相發明者，言雖不同，道則未始有異也。苟徒于其言，而不于其心，何足以論一中之妙於千古之上乎？愚未聞道也，道統之傳，不敢妄議。請因執事之問而言之。禮者，天理之節文；義者，人心之裁制。配乎天，則爲亨、爲利，而分四時；屬乎人，則合仁與智，而爲四德。若夫有分辨之廉，有羞惡之耻，固非出乎禮義之外也。故人有禮義者，必有廉耻；無廉耻者，必無禮義。則廉耻者，誠禮義中之一事，大德中之小節耳。舉禮義並仁智而稱四德，可也；推廉耻抗禮義而稱
translation_en:
…Liu Zihou once advanced this argument. This essay expounds it with gratifying clarity, enough to dispel every doubt. Were Zihou to return to life, he would surely consider me someone who understands his words!

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: Answers like this to a policy question on ritual propriety and righteousness are exceedingly rare.

Comment by Examiner Sun, School Instructor: This is writing that analyzes principle.

Those who discuss well the transmission of the succession of the Way attend not merely to the sages’ words, but necessarily to their minds. The Way originates in Heaven and is fully present in the human mind. What their minds share is the same Way. All the sages’ words serve to illuminate the Way, yet some elucidate one another: although their words differ, the Way has never differed. If one attends merely to their words and not to their minds, how can one adequately discuss the subtlety of the single Mean in remotest antiquity? I, in my ignorance, have not learned the Way and dare not speak recklessly about its transmission. Permit me to address it in response to your question.

Ritual propriety is the ordered articulation of Heaven’s principle; righteousness is the human mind’s capacity to judge and determine what is fitting. In their correspondence with Heaven, they constitute flourishing and benefit, taking their respective places among the four seasons; in their relation to humanity, they join benevolence and wisdom to constitute the four virtues. As for integrity, with its capacity to distinguish, and a sense of shame, with its shame at and aversion to wrongdoing, these certainly do not lie outside ritual propriety and righteousness. Thus, anyone possessing ritual propriety and righteousness necessarily possesses integrity and a sense of shame; anyone lacking integrity and a sense of shame necessarily lacks ritual propriety and righteousness. Integrity and a sense of shame are therefore indeed particular aspects of ritual propriety and righteousness, minor observances within the greater virtues. It is acceptable to place ritual propriety and righteousness alongside benevolence and wisdom and call them the four virtues; but to elevate integrity and a sense of shame to equal standing with ritual propriety and righteousness and call them…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
四維可乎柳宗元雖未為知道其論管子
為失言是矣真西山雖號稱儒者其以管
子為未可非則誤也且禮義者人所稟於
天之性也其為體也不偏不倚其為用也
無過不及此允執厥中之言堯得之天而
舜得之堯也顧雖上智不能無人心雖下
愚不能無道心故精以察之一以守之則
人心以安道心以著惡有非禮之禮非義
之義哉此禹之所以得統於舜也成湯懋
===
昭大德建中于民蓋能以義制事以禮制
心則事得其宜而心得其正惡有察之不
精守之不一哉此湯之所以得統於禹也
文王純一之德詠于思齊之詩則曰不顯
亦臨無射亦保又曰不聞亦式不諫亦入
夫亦臨亦保即湯制心之禮亦式亦入即
湯制事之義一德相承豈復有毫釐之差
哉武王受丹書之戒則曰敬勝怠者吉義
勝欲者從周公繫易爻之辭則曰敬以直
punctuated: 四維可乎？柳宗元雖未為知道，其論管子為失言，是矣。真西山雖號稱儒者，其以管子為未可非，則誤也。且禮義者，人所稟於天之性也。其為體也，不偏不倚；其為用也，無過不及。此「允執厥中」之言，堯得之天，而舜得之堯也。顧雖上智不能無人心，雖下愚不能無道心，故精以察之，一以守之，則人心以安，道心以著，惡有非禮之禮、非義之義哉？此禹之所以得統於舜也。成湯懋昭大德，建中于民，蓋能以義制事，以禮制心，則事得其宜，而心得其正，惡有察之不精、守之不一哉？此湯之所以得統於禹也。文王純一之德，詠于《思齊》之詩，則曰：「不顯亦臨，無射亦保。」又曰：「不聞亦式，不諫亦入。」夫亦臨亦保，即湯制心之禮；亦式亦入，即湯制事之義。一德相承，豈復有毫釐之差哉？武王受丹書之戒，則曰：「敬勝怠者吉，義勝欲者從。」周公繫易爻之辭，則曰：「敬以直
translation_en:
…can they be called the Four Bonds? Although Liu Zongyuan cannot be said to have understood the Way, he was right to judge Guanzi’s statement mistaken. Although Zhen Xishan was reputed to be a Confucian scholar, he was wrong to hold that Guanzi could not be faulted. Ritual propriety and righteousness are the nature that human beings receive from Heaven. In their substance, they incline to neither side; in their operation, they neither exceed nor fall short. This is the meaning of “Sincerely hold fast to the Mean”: Yao received it from Heaven, and Shun received it from Yao. Yet even the wisest cannot be without the human mind, and even the most foolish cannot be without the mind of the Way. Thus, by discerning them with precision and holding fast with single-mindedness, the human mind is settled and the mind of the Way becomes manifest. How could there then be propriety that violates propriety, or righteousness that violates righteousness? This is how Yu inherited the succession from Shun.

Cheng Tang strove to manifest his great virtue and established the Mean among the people. He could regulate affairs through righteousness and regulate the mind through ritual propriety; thus affairs attained their fitting order and the mind attained its rectitude. How could his discernment have lacked precision, or his adherence have lacked single-mindedness? This is how Tang inherited the succession from Yu.

King Wen’s pure and undivided virtue is celebrated in the ode “Si Qi” (“Thinking of the Dignified One”), which says: “Even where unseen, he felt a presence above him; without wearying, he maintained his vigilance.” It also says: “Without instruction, he followed the model; without remonstrance, he entered the right path.” Feeling that presence and maintaining vigilance are precisely the ritual propriety by which Tang regulated his mind; following the model and entering the right path are precisely the righteousness by which Tang regulated affairs. As this single virtue passed from one to another, how could there have been even the slightest discrepancy?

King Wu received the admonition of the Cinnabar Writing, which says: “When reverence overcomes indolence, there is good fortune; when righteousness overcomes desire, things proceed favorably.” The Duke of Zhou appended the statements to the lines of the Book of Changes, saying: “Through reverence, straighten…”

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
内義以方外夫謂之敬者即文王之制心
謂之義者即文王之制事一心相授豈復
有先後之間哉若吾夫子得統於文武周
公其進以禮其退以義禮義未嘗不兼也
至於教人曰克己復禮則欲盡而禮還博
文約禮則知盡而行至干以馴致夫精義
入神之地不言義而義在其中矣孟子得
統於孔子以義為路以禮為門禮義未嘗
不該也至論養氣曰生由集義則動息有
===
養取非義襲則物我不留于以優入于周
旋中禮之域不言禮而禮在其中矣是知
群聖之言明載於書者雖若不同群聖之
道默傳於心者初無二致故曰前聖後聖
其揆一也勉齋黃氏親得朱子之傳蓋亦
有志於道統者其言豈無謂哉嗚呼群聖
邈矣其書固在也今天下之號為士者莫
不皆誦其書也而能得其傳者誰歟此執
事所以有憂而下問也愚竊有志焉柰之
punctuated: 内，義以方外。夫謂之敬者，即文王之制心；謂之義者，即文王之制事。一心相授，豈復有先後之間哉？若吾夫子得統於文武周公，其進以禮，其退以義，禮義未嘗不兼也。至於教人，曰克己復禮，則欲盡而禮還；博文約禮，則知盡而行至，干以馴致夫精義入神之地。不言義，而義在其中矣。孟子得統於孔子，以義為路，以禮為門，禮義未嘗不該也。至論養氣，曰生由集義，則動息有養；取非義襲，則物我不留，于以優入于周旋中禮之域。不言禮，而禮在其中矣。是知群聖之言，明載於書者，雖若不同；群聖之道，默傳於心者，初無二致。故曰：「前聖後聖，其揆一也。」勉齋黃氏親得朱子之傳，蓋亦有志於道統者，其言豈無謂哉？嗚呼！群聖邈矣，其書固在也。今天下之號為士者，莫不皆誦其書也，而能得其傳者誰歟？此執事所以有憂而下問也。愚竊有志焉，柰之
translation_en:
…within, and righteousness to square what is without.” What is called reverence is precisely King Wen’s regulation of the mind; what is called righteousness is precisely King Wen’s regulation of affairs. With this single mind transmitted from one to another, how could there be any distinction between earlier and later sages? Our Master Confucius inherited the succession from King Wen, King Wu, and the Duke of Zhou. He advanced according to ritual propriety and withdrew according to righteousness: he always embraced both. When teaching others, he said, “Overcome the self and return to ritual propriety”: selfish desires are exhausted and ritual propriety restored. “Broaden learning through literature and restrain it through ritual propriety”: knowledge is fully extended and conduct reaches its utmost, thereby gradually attaining the realm of refining righteousness and penetrating the spiritual [?]. Though he did not speak of righteousness, righteousness was contained therein. Mengzi inherited the succession from Confucius. He took righteousness as his road and ritual propriety as his gate, always encompassing both. When discussing the nourishment of vital energy, he said that it arises through the accumulation of righteousness, so that it is nourished in activity and rest; it is not seized through an isolated righteous act [?], so that neither external things nor the self cause obstruction. Thus one may enter with ease the realm in which every movement accords with ritual propriety. Though he did not speak of ritual propriety, ritual propriety was contained therein.
From this we know that although the words of the sages, plainly recorded in books, may seem different, their Way, silently transmitted from mind to mind, has never differed. Thus it is said: “The earlier sages and the later sages share the same standard.” Huang Mianzhai personally received Master Zhu’s transmission and was surely also devoted to the succession of the Way. Could his words have been without purpose? Alas! The sages are far removed from us, but their books remain. Today, all those under Heaven who call themselves scholars recite those books; yet who among them can receive their transmission? This is why you, honored examiner, are concerned and have condescended to put this question to us. I, in my ignorance, privately aspire to this, yet how…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
何未得其門而入也今惟篤守禮義之訓
以上遡精一之傳儻少有所得而免乎童
習白紛之誚皆執事之教也幸勿以爲不
知量云
第三問
鄭宗古
同考試官教諭粘批文章遲速窮達本非所計主
司設爲此問正欲觀諸士子志向如何子能脫去問目而卓然以
道立說三復之嘆服自不容已昔歐陽公讀東坡文亟口稱之
===
至欲讓出一頭地吾於子之是篇亦云
同考試官教諭張批雕蟲末技於道未尊世俗以遲
速窮達爲言甚悖於道也此篇提出道字以掃遲速窮達之
說如奏黃鍾大呂而天下之俗樂盡廢矣得士如此可
不爲科目慶邪
考試官教諭劉批詞嚴誼正觀此知子之學術
考試官學正孫批擅場之作
文以載道外道而爲文君子不取也蓋文
苟合乎道矣其思之遲速時之窮達固不
punctuated:
何未得其門而入也。今惟篤守禮義之訓，以上遡精一之傳，儻少有所得，而免乎童習白紛之誚，皆執事之教也。幸勿以爲不知量云。
第三問
鄭宗古
同考試官教諭粘批：文章遲速窮達，本非所計。主司設爲此問，正欲觀諸士子志向如何。子能脫去問目，而卓然以道立說，三復之，嘆服自不容已。昔歐陽公讀東坡文，亟口稱之，至欲讓出一頭地。吾於子之是篇亦云。
同考試官教諭張批：雕蟲末技，於道未尊。世俗以遲速窮達爲言，甚悖於道也。此篇提出道字，以掃遲速窮達之說，如奏黃鍾大呂，而天下之俗樂盡廢矣。得士如此，可不爲科目慶邪？
考試官教諭劉批：詞嚴誼正，觀此知子之學術。
考試官學正孫批：擅場之作。
文以載道，外道而爲文，君子不取也。蓋文苟合乎道矣，其思之遲速，時之窮達，固不
translation_en:
…yet how is it that I have not found the gate and entered? For now, I can only steadfastly uphold the teachings of ritual propriety and righteousness, tracing them back to the transmission of refinement and single-mindedness. If I gain some small understanding and escape the reproach of remaining mired in childhood learning into white-haired old age [?], it will all be owing to your instruction. I hope you will not consider me presumptuous.
Third Question
Zheng Zonggu
Comment by Associate Examiner Nian, Instructor: Speed or slowness in composition, and adversity or success in one's career, are fundamentally not matters to calculate. The chief examiners devised this question precisely to discern the aspirations of the candidates. You have been able to move beyond the question's terms and establish your argument firmly upon the Way. Reading it three times, I could not restrain my admiration. When Master Ouyang read Dongpo's writing, he praised it repeatedly, even wishing to yield him the foremost place. I would say the same of this essay of yours.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: Literary ornament is a minor skill and does not accord the Way its due eminence. The vulgar preoccupation with speed or slowness, adversity or success, runs profoundly counter to the Way. This essay brings forward the word “Way” to sweep aside such discussions, like sounding the Huangzhong and Dalu pitch standards and thereby silencing all the world's vulgar music. When men of this caliber are selected, how could one fail to rejoice for the examination system?
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: Your language is rigorous and your meaning correct. This reveals the character of your learning.
Comment by Examiner Sun, School Instructor: A work that surpasses all others in the field.
Writing serves to convey the Way. The gentleman does not accept writing composed apart from the Way. For if writing accords with the Way, then the speed or slowness of its conception, and the adversity or success encountered in its time, certainly need not…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
必言苟戾乎道矣其思之遲速時之窮達
亦不足論苟不以道而惟文之評喋喋於
孰遲孰速之辯切切於或窮或達之疑夫
辯其遲速是求工之心也疑其窮達是計
利之心也求工而計利為文之弊一至於
此哉執事棘闈取士正大振雅道之秋顧
乃以文思之遲速文人之窮達為問是豈
其溺於文哉愚固知覘諸生之志向也且
文思之速本乎天資若呂思禮作露布而
===
食頃即成王勃作滕王閣序而援筆立就
倚馬而萬言可待李太白也擊鉢而四韻
如神蕭文琰也當食草奏有若禰衡七步
賦詩有若曹植思如涌泉有若蘇頲文如
宿構有若王粲速可嘉矣於道槩乎未明
也夫何貴於速哉文思之遲亦本乎天資
若左思作三都賦而構思十年張衡作兩
京賦而鍊句一紀疾感於苦思者桓譚也
氣竭於沉慮者王充也濡筆腐毫有若相
punctuated: 必言。苟戾乎道矣，其思之遲速、時之窮達亦不足論。苟不以道而惟文之評，喋喋於孰遲孰速之辯，切切於或窮或達之疑，夫辯其遲速，是求工之心也；疑其窮達，是計利之心也。求工而計利，為文之弊一至於此哉！執事棘闈取士，正大振雅道之秋，顧乃以文思之遲速、文人之窮達為問，是豈其溺於文哉？愚固知覘諸生之志向也。且文思之速，本乎天資。若呂思禮作露布而食頃即成，王勃作《滕王閣序》而援筆立就，倚馬而萬言可待，李太白也；擊鉢而四韻如神，蕭文琰也；當食草奏，有若禰衡；七步賦詩，有若曹植；思如涌泉，有若蘇頲；文如宿構，有若王粲。速可嘉矣，於道槩乎未明也，夫何貴於速哉？文思之遲，亦本乎天資。若左思作《三都賦》而構思十年，張衡作《兩京賦》而鍊句一紀，疾感於苦思者，桓譚也；氣竭於沉慮者，王充也；濡筆腐毫，有若相
translation_en:
…need be discussed. If writing runs counter to the Way, neither the slowness or speed of its conception nor its author's adversity or success merits discussion either. If one judges writing solely as writing, without reference to the Way, endlessly debating who composes slowly and who quickly, and anxiously wondering why some suffer adversity while others achieve success, then debating their speed betrays a desire for technical accomplishment, while questioning their fortunes betrays a calculation of personal advantage. To seek accomplishment and calculate advantage—have the abuses of literary composition reached such a pass! You, sir, are selecting scholars within the examination compound: this is precisely the occasion to revive the proper literary tradition. Yet you ask about the speed of literary conception and the adversity or success of writers. Could this mean that you are engrossed in mere literary accomplishment? I know full well that you are probing the aspirations of us candidates.

Now, speed of literary conception rests upon natural endowment. Lü Sili composed a military proclamation in the time it takes to eat a meal; Wang Bo took up his brush and immediately completed the Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng. Li Taibai could produce ten thousand words while leaning against a horse, with scarcely any waiting; Xiao Wenyan [?] composed a poem of four rhymes with wondrous speed within the time marked by striking a bowl. Mi Heng drafted a memorial while eating; Cao Zhi composed a poem in seven paces. Su Ting's thoughts flowed like a bubbling spring; Wang Can's writing seemed to have been composed beforehand. Such speed is praiseworthy, but these writers seem not to have understood the Way. What, then, is so valuable about speed?

Slowness of literary conception likewise rests upon natural endowment. Zuo Si spent ten years devising his Rhapsodies on the Three Capitals; Zhang Heng spent twelve years refining the lines of his Rhapsodies on the Two Capitals. Huan Tan fell ill from arduous thought; Wang Chong exhausted his vital energy in deep deliberation. As for moistening the brush until its hairs decayed, there was Xiang…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
如輟翰驚夢有若揚雄閉門覓句有若陳
無已空齋卧思有若薛道衡遲則工矣於
道亦未之得也又何取於遲哉文能窮人
古人蓋有是論矣王欽若寄身幕府而因
詩召見後之登相此其權輿也陳簡齋分
教輔郡而因詩入對掌符之遷此其根本
也李太白作樂府而梨園被之管絃翰林
何增重歟楊徽之獻詩篇而太宗書之御
屏侍讀何馳名歟由此觀之文曷嘗盡能
===
窮人邪文能達人古人亦有是言矣孟浩
然隨王維直宿幸見明皇因詩忤而放歸
誠可恨也賈閬仙爲法乾寺僧幸遇宣宗
拜司倉而遽卒良可悲也劉夢得坐種桃
之句黜刺連州何途窮歟白樂天坐新井
之篇左遷湓浦何命薄歟由此觀之文曷
嘗盡能達人邪大抵君子所講者惟道所
行者惟道所傳於後世者惟道文之速固
不必矜文之遲亦不必計也時之達固可
punctuated: 如。輟翰驚夢，有若揚雄；閉門覓句，有若陳無已；空齋卧思，有若薛道衡。遲則工矣，於道亦未之得也，又何取於遲哉？文能窮人，古人蓋有是論矣。王欽若寄身幕府，而因詩召見，後之登相，此其權輿也。陳簡齋分教輔郡，而因詩入對，掌符之遷，此其根本也。李太白作樂府，而梨園被之管絃，翰林何增重歟！楊徽之獻詩篇，而太宗書之御屏，侍讀何馳名歟！由此觀之，文曷嘗盡能窮人邪？文能達人，古人亦有是言矣。孟浩然隨王維直宿，幸見明皇，因詩忤而放歸，誠可恨也。賈閬仙爲法乾寺僧，幸遇宣宗，拜司倉而遽卒，良可悲也。劉夢得坐種桃之句，黜刺連州，何途窮歟！白樂天坐新井之篇，左遷湓浦，何命薄歟！由此觀之，文曷嘗盡能達人邪？大抵君子所講者惟道，所行者惟道，所傳於後世者惟道。文之速固不必矜，文之遲亦不必計也。時之達固可
translation_en:
…[Sima Xiang]ru. There was Yang Xiong, who laid down his brush and was startled from a dream; Chen Wuyi, who shut his door to seek out lines of verse; and Xue Daoheng, who lay pondering in an empty study. Slowness may produce fine workmanship, yet these writers likewise failed to apprehend the Way. What, then, is there to prize in slowness?

The ancients did indeed argue that literary writing can bring a person to straitened circumstances. Yet Wang Qinruo, while serving on a staff, was summoned to an imperial audience because of his poetry: this was the beginning of his eventual rise to chief minister. Chen Jianzhai, while serving as an instructor in a prefecture near the capital, was called to answer the emperor because of his poetry: this laid the foundation for his promotion to an office bearing an official seal. Li Taibai composed Music Bureau songs, and the Pear Garden musicians set them to strings and winds: how greatly this enhanced the prestige of the Hanlin Academician! Yang Huizhi presented poems, and Emperor Taizong had them inscribed on his imperial screen: how widely this spread the fame of the Academician Reader-in-waiting! Seen in this light, how could literary writing invariably bring people to straitened circumstances?

The ancients also said that literary writing can bring a person advancement. Yet Meng Haoran accompanied Wang Wei on overnight duty and had the good fortune to meet Emperor Minghuang, only to offend him with a poem and be sent home. Truly regrettable! Jia Langxian was a monk at Faqian Temple and had the good fortune to encounter Emperor Xuanzong; he was appointed granary administrator but died soon afterward. Truly lamentable! Liu Mengde, on account of his lines about planting peach trees, was demoted to prefect of Lianzhou: how completely his prospects were blocked! Bai Letian, on account of his poem “New Well” [?], was demoted and sent to Penpu: how ill-fated he was! Seen in this light, how could literary writing invariably bring people advancement?

In general, what the gentleman studies is solely the Way; what he practices is solely the Way; and what he transmits to later generations is solely the Way. There is certainly no need to boast of speed in writing, nor any need to concern oneself with slowness. When circumstances permit advancement, one can certainly…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
兼善時之窮亦可獨善也愚雖不敏尚願
潜心於理學之淵源而弗敢喪志於詞章
之枝葉先本後末歛華就實不得已而或
有所述以鳴我
國家文明之盛决不敢計其遲與速窮與達
也惟執事不以為狂進而教之焉幸甚
第四問
嚴志迪
同考試官教諭武批此策以古人事跡相類者為
===
問場中間有能記者而文體冗亂漫無紀律或筆勢可觀
而又不能記亦不過敷衍成篇而已連日較閱深以不
得士為懼兹得此卷不惟條答無遺而文字整嚴無
一贅語策手也
考試官教諭劉批多識而有斷博雅之士也
考試官學正孫批峭拔
事之在天下異勢而同理者謂之同可也
同行而異情者謂之不同可也知其同不
同之迹者考諸史斷其同不同之理者本
punctuated:
兼善，時之窮亦可獨善也。愚雖不敏，尚願潜心於理學之淵源，而弗敢喪志於詞章之枝葉。先本後末，歛華就實，不得已而或有所述，以鳴我國家文明之盛，决不敢計其遲與速、窮與達也。惟執事不以為狂，進而教之焉，幸甚。

第四問
嚴志迪

同考試官教諭武批：此策以古人事跡相類者為問，場中間有能記者，而文體冗亂，漫無紀律；或筆勢可觀，而又不能記，亦不過敷衍成篇而已。連日較閱，深以不得士為懼。兹得此卷，不惟條答無遺，而文字整嚴，無一贅語，策手也。

考試官教諭劉批：多識而有斷，博雅之士也。

考試官學正孫批：峭拔。

事之在天下，異勢而同理者，謂之同可也；同行而異情者，謂之不同可也。知其同不同之迹者，考諸史；斷其同不同之理者，本
translation_en:
…benefit others as well as oneself; when circumstances are adverse, one may also cultivate goodness in oneself alone. Though I am slow of understanding, I still wish to devote myself to the wellsprings of the learning of principle, and dare not lose my purpose amid the branches and leaves of literary composition. Putting the root before the branches, restraining ornament and attending to substance, I may occasionally write when compelled to do so, to proclaim the flourishing literary culture of our state. I would never dare calculate whether my progress is slow or swift, or whether I meet adversity or success. If you, sir, do not consider me presumptuous, but admit me to your instruction, I shall be most fortunate.

Fourth Question
Yan Zhidi

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: This policy question takes similar incidents in the lives of men of antiquity as its subject. Among the candidates, some could recall them, but their writing was verbose and confused, utterly lacking order. Others displayed an admirable force of expression but could not recall the incidents, and merely padded their responses into complete essays. After several days of comparative reading, I was deeply concerned that we would find no worthy candidates. Now I have obtained this script: not only does it answer every item without omission, but its writing is orderly and rigorous, without a single superfluous phrase. Here is a master of the policy essay.

Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: Widely knowledgeable and possessed of sound judgment—a man of broad learning and refinement.

Comment by Examiner Sun, Instructor: Lofty and incisive.

Among the affairs of the world, those that differ in circumstances but share the same principle may be called alike; those that involve the same conduct but differ in underlying motives may be called unlike. To understand the outward evidence of their likeness or difference, one examines the histories; to judge the principles underlying their likeness or difference, one takes as one’s foundation…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
諸心善評人物者豈可泥其迹而不究其
心哉請因明問而對之所謂社稷臣者惟
汲黯可以當之武帝許之是也瑀則忠於
後而失於前普則忠於前而失於後果若
是耶乎所謂國士者雖李陵亦有所愧司
馬遷許之過也羽報效曹操飛義釋嚴顔
其殆庶幾乎蘇章張鎭周裴垍不私故人
之事雖異而同於守國法馬援王昶柳玭
教子之言雖殊而同於謹家教秦孝公聞
===
霸道於商鞅漢文帝聞鬼神於賈誼均非
朝廷之先務也其前席也奚益子產鑄刑
書於鄭趙鞅鑄刑鼎於晉均非德教之良
圖也於鄭晉也何補伊川勸尹和靖舉進
士而和靖不從時可以止而止是所見之
高也或勸桑維翰無舉進士而維翰不從
不宜沮而不沮是所志之定也王陵之母
不顧身之死以全其子移孝於忠母之死
何烈也趙括之母不顧子之死以全其身
punctuated: 諸心。善評人物者，豈可泥其迹而不究其心哉？請因明問而對之。所謂社稷臣者，惟汲黯可以當之，武帝許之是也。瑀則忠於後而失於前，普則忠於前而失於後，果若是耶乎？所謂國士者，雖李陵亦有所愧，司馬遷許之過也。羽報效曹操，飛義釋嚴顔，其殆庶幾乎！蘇章、張鎭周、裴垍不私故人之事雖異，而同於守國法；馬援、王昶、柳玭教子之言雖殊，而同於謹家教。秦孝公聞霸道於商鞅，漢文帝聞鬼神於賈誼，均非朝廷之先務也，其前席也奚益？子產鑄刑書於鄭，趙鞅鑄刑鼎於晉，均非德教之良圖也，於鄭、晉也何補？伊川勸尹和靖舉進士，而和靖不從，時可以止而止，是所見之高也。或勸桑維翰無舉進士，而維翰不從，不宜沮而不沮，是所志之定也。王陵之母不顧身之死以全其子，移孝於忠，母之死何烈也！趙括之母不顧子之死以全其身，
translation_en:
…on the heart. How could someone skilled at judging people cling to their outward deeds without examining their intentions? Permit me to reply in accordance with your discerning questions. As for the designation “minister who safeguards the state,” only Ji An deserves it; Emperor Wu was right to accord it to him. Yu 瑀 was loyal in his later years but at fault earlier, while Pu 普 was loyal earlier but at fault later: was this truly so? As for the designation “outstanding man of the realm,” even Li Ling fell short of it; Sima Qian went too far in according it to him. Guan Yu repaid Cao Cao’s kindness with service, and Zhang Fei acted righteously in releasing Yan Yan: did they not come close to deserving this designation?

Although the circumstances in which Su Zhang, Zhang Zhenzhou, and Pei Ji refused to favor old friends differed, they were alike in upholding the laws of the state. Although Ma Yuan, Wang Chang, and Liu Pian offered different counsel to their sons, they were alike in taking care over instruction within the family. Duke Xiao of Qin heard Shang Yang expound the way of the hegemon, and Emperor Wen of Han heard Jia Yi discuss ghosts and spirits. Neither subject was among the court’s foremost concerns: what benefit was there in moving forward on their seats to listen? Zichan cast the penal code in metal in Zheng, and Zhao Yang cast a cauldron bearing penal statutes in Jin. Neither was a sound plan for moral instruction: what benefit did these bring to Zheng and Jin?

Yichuan urged Yin Hejing to sit for the jinshi examinations, but Hejing did not follow his advice. When circumstances permitted withdrawal, he withdrew: this shows the loftiness of his insight. Someone urged Sang Weihan not to sit for the jinshi examinations, but Weihan did not follow that advice. When he ought not to have been discouraged, he remained undeterred: this shows the firmness of his resolve. Wang Ling’s mother disregarded her own death to preserve her son, directing his filial devotion toward loyalty to his ruler. How heroic was his mother’s death! Zhao Kuo’s mother disregarded her son’s death to preserve herself…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
諫王不聽母之生非忍也斷織勉學樂羊
子因妻而感奮可也以亞聖之才亦待斷
機而後成乎此蓋出於好事者之言無疑
矣多請田宅王翦術君以自汙固也以吳
漢之賢孰謂不買田宅之非真乎此蓋成
於尚名節之世有由矣李英公之守幷州
而恃於長城顏魯公之在河朔而恃於金
城所謂固國不以山谿之險者歟德宗欲
相裴延齡而陽城欲壞白麻文宗欲相鄭
===
注而李甘欲壞白麻所謂匹夫不可奪志
者歟馮驩李士謙之焚券同一輕利之心
要之士謙自焚其券不若馮驩焚薛券之
尤難也孟明杜詩之焚舟同一敢死之志
要之杜詩之討楊異不若孟明伐晉師之
尤難也孔子不飲盜泉之水者惡盜之名
吳隱之飲貪泉之水者破俗之忌也秦不
喜詩書而亡者有不喜之實漢不喜詩書
而興者有不喜之名也執事之所問者如
punctuated: 諫王不聽，母之生非忍也。斷織勉學，樂羊子因妻而感奮，可也；以亞聖之才，亦待斷機而後成乎？此蓋出於好事者之言，無疑矣。多請田宅，王翦術君以自汙，固也；以吳漢之賢，孰謂不買田宅之非真乎？此蓋成於尚名節之世，有由矣。李英公之守幷州而恃於長城，顏魯公之在河朔而恃於金城，所謂固國不以山谿之險者歟？德宗欲相裴延齡，而陽城欲壞白麻；文宗欲相鄭注，而李甘欲壞白麻，所謂匹夫不可奪志者歟？馮驩、李士謙之焚券，同一輕利之心；要之，士謙自焚其券，不若馮驩焚薛券之尤難也。孟明、杜詩之焚舟，同一敢死之志；要之，杜詩之討楊異，不若孟明伐晉師之尤難也。孔子不飲盜泉之水者，惡盜之名；吳隱之飲貪泉之水者，破俗之忌也。秦不喜詩書而亡者，有不喜之實；漢不喜詩書而興者，有不喜之名也。執事之所問者如
translation_en:
…she remonstrated with the king, but he would not listen; the mother’s survival was no act of heartlessness. As for cutting woven cloth to encourage study, it is plausible that Yue Yangzi was stirred to renewed effort by his wife. But could someone with the talents of the Second Sage, Mengzi, also have needed the cloth on the loom to be cut before achieving success? This undoubtedly originated in the words of someone fond of inventing stories. That Wang Jian repeatedly requested fields and residences as a means of managing his ruler by sullying his own reputation is certainly true. But given Wu Han’s worthiness, who could say that his refusal to purchase fields and residences was insincere? There was a reason why such conduct arose in an age that esteemed reputation and integrity.

When Li, Duke of Ying, guarded Bingzhou, he was relied upon as a great wall; when Yan, Duke of Lu, was in Heshuo, he was relied upon as a rampart of metal. Is this what is meant by saying that securing a state does not depend upon the natural defenses of mountains and ravines? When Dezong wished to appoint Pei Yanling chief councilor, Yang Cheng wanted to destroy the appointment edict on white hemp paper; when Wenzong wished to appoint Zheng Zhu chief councilor, Li Gan wanted to destroy such an edict. Is this what is meant by saying that even an ordinary man cannot be deprived of his resolve?

Feng Huan and Li Shiqian burned debt contracts with the same disregard for profit. Yet, in the final reckoning, Li Shiqian’s burning of his own contracts was less difficult than Feng Huan’s burning of the contracts for debts in Xue. Mengming and Du Shi burned their boats with the same resolve to risk death. Yet, in the final reckoning, Du Shi’s campaign against Yang Yi was less difficult than Mengming’s attack on the army of Jin. Kongzi refused to drink the water of Daoquan, the Robber Spring, because he abhorred the name ‘robber’; Wu Yinzhi drank the water of Tanquan, the Spring of Greed, to break a popular taboo. Qin disliked the Odes and the Documents and perished: its dislike was real. Han disliked the Odes and the Documents and rose: its dislike was merely reputed. What you, sir, have asked is as…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
此抑愚又有說焉天下之事莫不有理天
下之理皆原於心事雖散於簡冊之至繁
理則具於吾心之至約持一心之理照萬
古之事未有不得陽秋之當者也否則歷
覽古今徒為玩物喪志而已豈君子窮理
之學哉敢以是而推廣執事之問
第五問
吳憲
同考試官教諭粘批此篇說理財之道惟在去其
===
所以害財者切中時弊非留心經濟者不能末復舉文
帝仁宗曁我
聖祖用財多而財不匱處寓意微婉迥出群對萬一
廟堂採納豈獨湖藩之幸邪
同考試官教諭張批五策俱善如長江大河一瀉
千里而此篇尤傑特過人唐人號劉長卿為五言長城子其
萬言之長城歟宜取之以冠本房
考試官教諭劉批篇末引宣公之言尤切要
考試官學正孫批有用之學
punctuated:
此。抑愚又有說焉：天下之事莫不有理，天下之理皆原於心。事雖散於簡冊之至繁，理則具於吾心之至約。持一心之理，照萬古之事，未有不得陽秋之當者也。否則歷覽古今，徒為玩物喪志而已，豈君子窮理之學哉？敢以是而推廣執事之問。
第五問
吳憲
同考試官教諭粘批：此篇說理財之道，惟在去其所以害財者，切中時弊，非留心經濟者不能。末復舉文帝、仁宗曁我聖祖用財多而財不匱處，寓意微婉，迥出群對。萬一廟堂採納，豈獨湖藩之幸邪？
同考試官教諭張批：五策俱善，如長江大河，一瀉千里，而此篇尤傑特過人。唐人號劉長卿為五言長城，子其萬言之長城歟？宜取之以冠本房。
考試官教諭劉批：篇末引宣公之言，尤切要。
考試官學正孫批：有用之學。
translation_en:
…such. Yet I, in my ignorance, have something further to say. Every affair under Heaven has its principle, and all principles under Heaven originate in the mind. Although affairs are scattered through books and records in the utmost profusion, their principles are contained within our minds in the utmost simplicity. By holding to the principles of the single mind and illuminating the affairs of all ages, one invariably arrives at fitting judgments of praise and blame, as in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Otherwise, surveying past and present merely amounts to losing one’s resolve through fascination with external things. How could this be the gentleman’s learning that exhaustively investigates principle? I venture to offer this as an extension of your question.
Fifth Policy Question
Wu Xian
Comment by Associate Examiner Nian, Instructor: This essay argues that the way to manage finances lies solely in removing what harms them. It strikes directly at the abuses of our times; only someone attentive to statecraft could have written it. At the end, it further cites Emperor Wen, Emperor Renzong, and our Sagely Founder as instances of rulers whose expenditure was great yet whose resources were not exhausted. Its implications are subtle and tactful, and it far surpasses the other answers. Should the court happen to adopt its proposals, would Huguang alone be fortunate?
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: All five policy essays are excellent, flowing like the Yangzi and the Yellow River, sweeping a thousand li in a single surge. This essay is especially outstanding and surpasses the others. People of the Tang called Liu Changqing the Great Wall of five-character verse. Might you be the Great Wall of ten thousand words? This answer should be selected to head our examination section.
Comment by Examiner Liu, Instructor: The quotation from Duke Xuan at the end of the essay is especially pertinent and essential.
Comment by Examiner Sun, School Director: Learning of practical use.

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
理財之道無他焉亦曰惟去其所以害財
者而已矣夫天下之財歲聚於官者有定
額而給散之數日增焉無惑乎日益不足
也使事之害財者未去雖求財而益之財
愈不足若事之害財者旣去不求豐財而
財自豐矣昔人所謂去之甚易而無損存
之甚難而無益者其斯之謂乎執事以湖
藩財賦最急且大者爲問此
廟堂之深筭非草茅之士所與知也雖然一
===
得之愚弗容緘默請試陳之王制三年耕
必有一年之食九年耕必有三年之食以
三十年之通雖有凶旱水溢民無菜色然
後天子食日舉以樂蓋王者與民同患民
不安食不甘也周禮春官天府祭天之司
民司祿而獻民數穀數則受而藏之蓋獻
數者俾其知登耗多寡也故管子曰倉廩
實而知禮節賈誼曰積貯者天下之大命
由此觀之是財賦常宜有餘不宜不足也
punctuated:
理財之道無他焉，亦曰惟去其所以害財者而已矣。夫天下之財，歲聚於官者有定額，而給散之數日增焉，無惑乎日益不足也。使事之害財者未去，雖求財而益之，財愈不足；若事之害財者旣去，不求豐財而財自豐矣。昔人所謂「去之甚易而無損，存之甚難而無益」者，其斯之謂乎？執事以湖藩財賦最急且大者爲問，此廟堂之深筭，非草茅之士所與知也。雖然，一得之愚，弗容緘默，請試陳之。
《王制》：「三年耕，必有一年之食；九年耕，必有三年之食。以三十年之通，雖有凶旱水溢，民無菜色，然後天子食，日舉以樂。」蓋王者與民同患，民不安，食不甘也。《周禮》春官天府：「祭天之司民司祿而獻民數穀數，則受而藏之。」蓋獻數者，俾其知登耗多寡也。故《管子》曰：「倉廩實而知禮節。」賈誼曰：「積貯者，天下之大命。」由此觀之，是財賦常宜有餘，不宜不足也。
translation_en:
There is no other way to manage public finances than to remove what harms them. The wealth collected annually by the authorities throughout the realm has a fixed quota, while disbursements increase daily. It is no wonder that the shortfall grows ever greater. If practices that harm the finances remain, then even if additional revenue is sought and obtained, the resources become still less adequate. If those practices are removed, resources will become abundant of themselves, without any effort to increase them. Is this not what an earlier writer meant by saying, “Removing it is very easy and entails no loss; maintaining it is very difficult and brings no benefit”? You, honored examiners, have asked about the most urgent and consequential matters concerning Huguang’s revenues. These involve the court’s profound deliberations, which a scholar outside official service is not in a position to know. Nevertheless, even a foolish man may have one worthwhile insight, and I cannot remain silent. Allow me to set it forth.
The “Royal Regulations” chapter of the Book of Rites states: “Three years of cultivation must yield one year’s food reserve; nine years of cultivation must yield three years’ food reserve. Taking the balance over thirty years, even if there are disastrous droughts or floods, the people will show no signs of hunger. Only then does the Son of Heaven have his daily meal served with music.” For a true king shares the people’s troubles: when they are ill at ease, his food has no savor. The Rites of Zhou, in the section on the Celestial Treasury under the Ministry of Rites, states: “When sacrifices are offered to Heaven’s Director of the People and Director of Emoluments, and the population and grain figures are presented, it receives and stores them.” These figures are presented so that increases and losses, abundance and scarcity, may be known. Thus the Guanzi says: “When the granaries are full, people understand ritual and propriety.” Jia Yi says: “Accumulated reserves are the great lifeline of the realm.” From this we can see that public revenues should always be in surplus and never fall short.

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
今湖藩之在天下誠巨藩也我
聖祖均田定制歲收之額不過二百一十萬耳
今歲支之數多至二百二十萬焉縱使歲
皆有秋民皆無負而用猶不足誠有如執
事之所言者夫何邇年以來洪水為患
上俞撫臣之請至遣
廷臣發內帑借他省之羨餘開納銀之新例
而僅克有濟焉是豈其得已哉蓋一時權
宜之術也况湖之為省也
===
宗藩視天下諸省為多分封之漸蕃戚里之
彌盛將來方蔓衍而未已也壤地與蜀貴
江廣相接往年有筸子坪之征去年有郴
桂香爐之役將來恐用武之難免也夫
宗藩日盛則歲祿日增歲祿不可損也軍功
續錄則月俸荐加月俸不可減也斯時也
欲以二百一十萬之儲而供二百二十萬
之用而將來增加者又不可計雖使劉晏
度支李翺司計楊炎典籌亦末如之何也
punctuated: 今湖藩之在天下，誠巨藩也。我聖祖均田定制，歲收之額不過二百一十萬耳。今歲支之數，多至二百二十萬焉。縱使歲皆有秋，民皆無負，而用猶不足，誠有如執事之所言者。夫何邇年以來，洪水為患，上俞撫臣之請，至遣廷臣發內帑，借他省之羨餘，開納銀之新例，而僅克有濟焉。是豈其得已哉？蓋一時權宜之術也。况湖之為省也，宗藩視天下諸省為多，分封之漸蕃，戚里之彌盛，將來方蔓衍而未已也。壤地與蜀、貴、江、廣相接，往年有筸子坪之征，去年有郴、桂、香爐之役，將來恐用武之難免也。夫宗藩日盛，則歲祿日增，歲祿不可損也；軍功續錄，則月俸荐加，月俸不可減也。斯時也，欲以二百一十萬之儲，而供二百二十萬之用，而將來增加者又不可計，雖使劉晏度支，李翺司計，楊炎典籌，亦末如之何也。
translation_en:
Now Huguang is indeed a great province within the realm. Our sagely founding emperor equalized the landholdings and established the regulations; the prescribed annual revenue amounted to no more than 2,100,000. Yet annual expenditure now reaches as much as 2,200,000. Even if every year brought a good harvest and no one fell into arrears, the funds would still be insufficient—just as you, honored examiners, have said. Moreover, in recent years floods have caused such devastation that His Majesty approved the request of the Grand Coordinator and went so far as to dispatch court officials, release funds from the imperial treasury, borrow the surpluses of other provinces, and introduce new provisions for making payments in silver. Even then, these measures barely sufficed to provide relief. Could this have been done willingly? These were merely expedients for the moment.

Furthermore, Huguang has more establishments of imperial princes than the other provinces of the realm. As princely enfeoffments gradually multiply and the families of imperial relatives grow ever more numerous, they will continue to proliferate without end. Its territory adjoins Shu, Gui, Jiang, and Guang. In earlier years there was the expedition against Ganziping; last year there were the campaigns at Chen, Gui, and Xianglu. In the future, I fear, recourse to arms will be difficult to avoid. As the princely establishments grow, their annual stipends increase, and those stipends cannot be curtailed. As further military merit is entered on the rolls, monthly salaries repeatedly rise, and those salaries cannot be reduced. Under these circumstances, one seeks to meet expenditures of 2,200,000 from reserves of 2,100,000, while future increases cannot even be reckoned. Even if Liu Yan administered expenditure, Li Ao managed the accounts, and Yang Yan directed financial planning, they could do nothing about it…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
已矣然則為今之計柰何愚惟曰去其所
以害財者而已何謂害財曰冗官也冗兵
也冗役也之三者總而計之一日之費幾
何積日而為月一月之費幾何積月而為
歲一歲之費幾何因其一年之所支而通
計累年之所用則倉廩之匱乏生民之彫
敝有由然矣誠使冗食者去則歲之所入
足用而有餘倉之所儲先事而有備雖遇
水旱之變螟蝗之害盜賊之憂官府可以
===
從容處之而民不告瘁蘇東坡所謂天不
能使之災地不能使之貧盜賊不能使之
困者此之謂也由是平時而祿俸皆完矣
遇災而賑恤有備矣九年之蓄可以徐致
萬年之計可以永保其為我
國家之利何其大哉抑嘗有疑焉我
朝疆宇較之前代為甚廣而儲積當數倍也
漢初時有匈奴和親之繒黃河築塞之勞
邊徼出師之費財宜不充矣而文帝累下
punctuated:
已矣！然則為今之計柰何？愚惟曰：去其所以害財者而已。何謂害財？曰冗官也，冗兵也，冗役也。之三者，總而計之，一日之費幾何？積日而為月，一月之費幾何？積月而為歲，一歲之費幾何？因其一年之所支而通計累年之所用，則倉廩之匱乏、生民之彫敝，有由然矣。誠使冗食者去，則歲之所入足用而有餘，倉之所儲先事而有備。雖遇水旱之變、螟蝗之害、盜賊之憂，官府可以從容處之，而民不告瘁。蘇東坡所謂「天不能使之災，地不能使之貧，盜賊不能使之困」者，此之謂也。由是平時而祿俸皆完矣，遇災而賑恤有備矣。九年之蓄可以徐致，萬年之計可以永保，其為我國家之利何其大哉！

抑嘗有疑焉：我朝疆宇較之前代為甚廣，而儲積當數倍也。漢初時，有匈奴和親之繒、黃河築塞之勞、邊徼出師之費，財宜不充矣，而文帝累下
translation_en:
…That is all that can be done! What, then, should be our plan now? In my humble view, we need only eliminate what drains our resources. What drains them? Superfluous officials, superfluous soldiers, and superfluous service personnel. Taking these three together, how much do they cost in a single day? Accumulate the days into a month: how much do they cost in a month? Accumulate the months into a year: how much do they cost in a year? From the expenditure for one year, calculate the total spent over successive years, and the reasons for our empty granaries and the impoverishment of the people become clear. If those who consume resources unnecessarily were indeed removed, annual revenues would suffice for expenditure and leave a surplus, while grain stored in the granaries would provide reserves before emergencies arose. Even in the face of floods and droughts, destructive borers and locusts, or troubles caused by bandits, the authorities could respond at ease, and the people would not be reduced to distress. This is what Su Dongpo meant when he said: “Heaven cannot bring disaster upon them; earth cannot impoverish them; bandits cannot reduce them to hardship.” Thus, in ordinary times, stipends and salaries would all be paid in full, and when disaster struck, provisions for relief would be ready. Reserves sufficient for nine years could gradually be accumulated, and provision for ten thousand years could be secured forever. How great the benefit to our state would be!

Yet I have long had a doubt. Our dynasty’s territory is far more extensive than that of earlier dynasties, and its accumulated reserves ought to be several times greater. In the early Han, there were the silks supplied for marriage alliances with the Xiongnu, the labor of constructing embankments and closing breaches on the Yellow River, and the expense of sending armies to the frontiers. One would expect its resources to have been insufficient, yet Emperor Wen repeatedly issued…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
蠲租之詔焉宋有郊賚有歲幣有祠祿財
宜不充矣而仁宗減畿內諸縣之稅焉是
何也蓋文帝仁宗皆恭儉之主也朝無冗
食國有餘財此去其害財者之明效也我
聖祖建極之初正創制立度之始凡城池宮室
官署學校壇壝祠廟之費不可勝筭而免
稅之詔無歲無之蓋我
聖祖節用愛人尤非文帝仁宗所可擬者此所
以結人心凝
===
天命而培千萬年不拔之基也矧今
列聖重熙累洽之後我
皇上垂拱仰成不必別求理財之道也唯察其
害財者而去之則府庫自爾日盈災沴自
爾有備以之建功而功無不成以之興事
而事無不治尚何匱乏之足慮哉昔陸贄
告其君曰生物之豐敗由天用物之多少
由人是以先王立程量入爲出雖遇災難
下無困窮旨哉言乎誠萬世人君制用豐
punctuated:
蠲租之詔焉。宋有郊賚，有歲幣，有祠祿，財宜不充矣，而仁宗減畿內諸縣之稅焉，是何也？蓋文帝、仁宗皆恭儉之主也。朝無冗食，國有餘財，此去其害財者之明效也。我聖祖建極之初，正創制立度之始，凡城池、宮室、官署、學校、壇壝、祠廟之費，不可勝筭，而免稅之詔，無歲無之。蓋我聖祖節用愛人，尤非文帝、仁宗所可擬者。此所以結人心，凝天命，而培千萬年不拔之基也。
矧今列聖重熙累洽之後，我皇上垂拱仰成，不必別求理財之道也。唯察其害財者而去之，則府庫自爾日盈，災沴自爾有備。以之建功，而功無不成；以之興事，而事無不治。尚何匱乏之足慮哉？昔陸贄告其君曰：「生物之豐敗由天，用物之多少由人。是以先王立程，量入爲出，雖遇災難，下無困窮。」旨哉言乎！誠萬世人君制用豐
translation_en:
…edicts remitting agricultural taxes. The Song had largesse bestowed at the suburban sacrifices, annual tribute payments, and stipends for temple sinecures. Its finances should have been insufficient, yet Renzong reduced the taxes of the counties within the capital region. Why was this? Emperor Wen and Renzong were both reverent and frugal rulers. Their courts had no superfluous mouths to feed, and their states had surplus funds. This was the clear result of eliminating what harmed their finances. When our sagely founding ancestor first established sovereign rule, institutions and regulations were only beginning to be created. Expenditures on city walls and moats, palaces and other buildings, government offices, schools, sacrificial altars and their enclosures, and shrines and temples were beyond reckoning. Yet not a year passed without an edict granting tax exemptions. In his economy of expenditure and love for the people, our sagely founding ancestor far surpassed even Emperor Wen and Renzong. By these means he won the people's hearts, secured Heaven's Mandate, and laid a foundation that would stand unshaken for countless ages.
How much more is this so now, after successive sagely sovereigns have sustained prosperity and good government! Our Emperor need only sit with hands folded and rely on his ministers to accomplish their tasks; there is no need to seek some other way of managing the finances. He need only identify and eliminate what harms them. Then the treasuries will naturally grow fuller each day, and provision against calamities will naturally be assured. With these resources, no achievement he undertakes will fail, and no enterprise he initiates will go unmanaged. What shortage could still give cause for concern? Lu Zhi once told his ruler: “Whether production is abundant or fails depends on Heaven; whether consumption is great or small depends on people. Thus the former kings established standards and measured expenditure against income. Even when calamities occurred, those below suffered neither hardship nor destitution.” How profound these words are! Truly, for rulers of all ages, they are the essential way to regulate expenditure and increase…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text: 財之要道也敢以是復
punctuated: 財之要道也，敢以是復。
translation_en: …the essential way to enrich the treasury. I venture to submit this in reply.

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
湖廣鄉試錄後序
湖廣鄉試例取士八十五人
第其氏名擇其文之最純者
二十篇彙書為錄以薦聞于
上
制也我
國家政教旁達南極滇粤之間
===
前代所不能臣者皆立學校
被文教計以幅幀湖廣於今
日為中州地也故士之文亦
莫盛於今日正德己卯清濫
試事于兹則見夫多士之文
雄深俊逸渾厚典雅浹旬之
間如探萬玉之府取之無窮
punctuated:
湖廣鄉試錄後序

湖廣鄉試例取士八十五人，第其氏名，擇其文之最純者二十篇，彙書為錄，以薦聞于上，制也。

我國家政教旁達，南極滇粤之間，前代所不能臣者，皆立學校，被文教。計以幅幀，湖廣於今日為中州地也。故士之文亦莫盛於今日。正德己卯，清濫試事于兹，則見夫多士之文，雄深俊逸，渾厚典雅。浹旬之間，如探萬玉之府，取之無窮
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Huguang Provincial Examination

By established rule, the Huguang Provincial Examination selects eighty-five candidates. Their names are arranged in order of rank, and twenty of the finest essays are selected and compiled into a record for submission to the emperor. This is the prescribed procedure.

Our dynasty’s government and moral instruction extend in every direction, reaching southward to the regions of Dian and Yue. Even among those whom previous dynasties could not bring into subjection, schools have been established, and the people receive civilizing instruction. Judged by the territorial extent [?], Huguang today lies in the central region of the realm. Thus the candidates’ literary accomplishments, too, have never flourished more than they do today. In the jimao year of Zhengde [1519], I, Qing 清, was undeservedly entrusted with examination duties here. I found the many candidates’ writings powerful and profound, brilliant and untrammeled, substantial and dignified, classically refined. Over the course of ten days, it was as though I were exploring a treasury of myriad jades, drawing from it without end…

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
爲之目眩心動盖雖不能盡
錄而士之登名焉者可以槩
見之矣湖廣學校凡百四十
有二士極于萬且贏焉今所
取百不能一不可謂不難也
群超萃拔於一鄉之中遂以
策名
===
天朝而遍播天下不可謂不榮
也然古之所謂文者深涵而
富負經綸規畫彪炳而輝赫
孔子曰文不在茲乎非言辭
之謂也言且不足以盡文况
空言乎其文足以不朽而名
亦隨之書曰終有辭於永世
punctuated:
爲之目眩心動。盖雖不能盡錄，而士之登名焉者，可以槩見之矣。湖廣學校凡百四十有二，士極于萬且贏焉。今所取，百不能一，不可謂不難也。群超萃拔於一鄉之中，遂以策名天朝，而遍播天下，不可謂不榮也。
然古之所謂文者，深涵而富負，經綸規畫，彪炳而輝赫。孔子曰：「文不在茲乎？」非言辭之謂也。言且不足以盡文，况空言乎？其文足以不朽，而名亦隨之。《書》曰：「終有辭於永世。」
translation_en:
…dazzling the eyes and stirring the heart. Although these writings cannot all be recorded, those scholars whose names appear here afford a general view of them. Huguang has altogether 142 schools, and its scholars number more than ten thousand. Those now selected amount to fewer than one in a hundred: this can hardly be called easy. Having surpassed their fellows and distinguished themselves among the assembled scholars of a single province, they thus have their names inscribed at the imperial court and made known throughout the realm: this can hardly be called anything but an honor.
Yet what the ancients called “wen”—cultural accomplishment—was deeply cultivated and richly endowed, encompassing the ordering of affairs and the formulation of plans, brilliant and resplendent. Confucius said, “Does not this culture reside here in me?” He was not speaking of words alone. If even words cannot fully express cultural accomplishment, how much less can empty words? When a person's cultural accomplishment merits immortality, lasting fame follows it. The Book of Documents says, “In the end, you will be spoken of for all ages.”

title: 正德十四年湖廣鄉試錄
text:
言無窮也名不足以昭遠與
無名同况未核之名乎考之
唐虞敷奏考言期于厎績是
故功言俱立而名無窮焉苟
或以飾於外者自誣為已得
遇於人者□□□身榮是猶
矜宫□□□□□洋視溝澮
===
□□遍播天下不□以爲名
也至□□□所謂文章萃萬
狀□□□□□憂態不可勝
窮斯□□之至文也故澤被
海宇而秩隆百世諸士子生
長中土毓秀于洞庭衡嶽之
間豈其□詞章炫朝夕而已
punctuated: 言無窮也。名不足以昭遠，與無名同，况未核之名乎？考之唐虞，敷奏考言，期于厎績。是故功言俱立，而名無窮焉。苟或以飾於外者自誣為已得，遇於人者□□□身榮，是猶矜宫□□□□□洋視溝澮，□□遍播天下，不□以爲名也。至□□□所謂文章，萃萬狀□□□□□憂態，不可勝窮。斯□□之至文也。故澤被海宇，而秩隆百世。諸士子生長中土，毓秀于洞庭衡嶽之間，豈其□詞章炫朝夕而已？
translation_en: …This means that it has no end. A reputation insufficient to shine into the distant future is no different from having no reputation; how much more so a reputation not yet substantiated! Consider the age of Tang and Yu: men presented their reports and their words were examined, with the expectation that they would achieve results. Thus, achievements and words were both established, and their reputations endured without end. If someone deceives himself into thinking that outward embellishment constitutes attainment, and regards the recognition he receives from others as […] personal glory [?], this is like boasting of palaces […] and viewing drainage ditches […] [?]. […] Though spread throughout the world, this cannot [?] be considered a reputation. As for […] what is called literary accomplishment, it gathers together myriad forms […] states of sorrow [?], inexhaustible in their variety. This […] is the highest literary accomplishment. Hence its beneficence extends throughout the realm, and its honored standing endures for a hundred generations. You examination candidates were born and raised in the central lands, nurtured in excellence between Dongting and Mount Heng. Could you merely […] dazzle others for a brief moment with literary compositions?
